column4: Gender Analysis of AANR Technology Development Processes Towards Gender-Responsive Standards, Protocols and Assessment Tools
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: The Philippines has long subscribed to the principle and practice of gender mainstreaming to address issues of gender inequality and harness women’s empowerment, in all aspects of society. Hence, government institutions such as PCAARRD have endeavored to mainstream gender in its operations, including project development in the agricultural, aquatic and natural resources (AANR) sectors, where various studies have emphasized differences in women’s and men’s roles. Technological innovation, including machine development, in these sectors is not free from gendered assumptions about prospective users and the contexts for their technology utilization. Preconceived notions on gender roles impact on how technology is conceptualized and developed, perhaps more so in resource-based settings. Using gender analytical frames and gender-sensitive research methods, this proposed 2-year project would like to develop enabling mechanisms to make AANR technology development processes more gender responsive.

column4: Harvesting Tomorrow: Envisioning the Futures of the Luzon Semi-Temperate Vegetable Industry by 2050 through Strategic Foresight
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: The Philippine Vegetable Industry has a big growth potential but is currently beset with many challenges. A major transformation is necessary to make it into a resilient and sustainable sector. In a world of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity, hindsight and insight are not sufficient to navigate the future. Futures thinking and foresight become a necessary complement to the traditional planning process. The reactive responses to the challenges being experienced by the vegetable industry should be replaced by proactive policies. Problems and issues now could have been avoided if planning and efforts for the sector had been anticipatory. It is not too late; however, to change things and reimagine everything so that we can be prepared to face a future that is bleak or so that we can move easily towards this preferred future for the vegetable industry. This study will reimagine the country's semi-temperate/highland vegetable industry and propose actions toward a future-proof sector, i.e. sustainable and resilient against the unknowns, shocks, and disruptions.

column4: Value Chain Analysis of Pearl Oyster (Pteriidae) Towards Sustainable and Competitive Pearling Industry in the Philippines
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: This research proposal will assess the performance of the pearl oyster industry in the Philippines using the Value Chain Framework. Through this framework, the movement of the product, from input supply, production, postharvest, trade, and market will be characterized. Data will be collected through primary (focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and validation workshop that is well represented by stakeholders on all nodes across the value chain) and secondary data (e.g., Philippine Statistics Authority, Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, Local Government Units). The governance and socio-economic dimensions will be integrated with ecological measurements through different fisheries performance indicators. This will give a clear picture of the level of sustainability of the commodity, the resilience of the value chain, and information, which is vital in decision-making. Chain Performance Analysis will be used to evaluate the performance of existing supply/value chain in the pearl oyster industry (i.e., efficiency, flexibility, overall responsiveness).

column4: Reproductive Biology and Product Development in Rainbow Sardines, Dussumieria sp. (Teleostei:Clupeidae) from selected Marine Habitats in Western Visayas
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: The three-year project aims to re-evaluate existing information on the reproductive biology of rainbow sardines, Dussumieria spp. to support fish conservation efforts by the local coastal cities and municipalities bordering Iloilo Strait and the Visayan Sea. This project also aims to develop new food and pharmaceutical products with rainbow sardines as the main ingredient to efficiently used the fish resources in the region. Specifically, this project will (1) characterize gonadal development stages of the rainbow sardines based on histological observations, (2) describe the annual and diel/lunar gonadal cycle of the said species, (3) characterize the size and age at maturity, sex ratio, fecundity, and other relevant reproductive parameters, (4) develop food and pharmaceutical products out of rainbow sardines, and (5) engage local communities to produce high quality sardine products (Spanish style rainbow sardine and sardine candies) by establishing standard analytical tests for quality assurance including microbiological, biochemical and sensory evaluation protocols. The expected outputs include publication, patent, product, people service, place and partnership, and policy. The expected beneficiaries include marginal fisher folks, local government units, government agencies, fish consumers, and businessmen.

column4: Iron, Nickel, and Nitrate from Aerosol Deposition and their Influence on Growth and Toxin Production of Harmful Algal Bloom Species (IRON-HABs)
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: The occurrence of harmful algal blooms (HABs) causes financial losses for stakeholders, poses health risks to consumers, and disrupts the ecological balance where it ensues. In Bolinao, Pangasinan alone, the financial losses due to fish kill was estimated to be PhP 21.9 million in May 2020 and PhP 107 million in June 2018. The most devastating loss happened in February 2002 with reported loss valued at PhP 500 million. The financial losses alone highlight the importance of understanding the factors triggering the occurrence/recurrence of HABs. Aspects of HAB formation and persistence have been brought into light by excellent research conducted by various groups in the country. Despite this, the complex nature of photosynthetic organisms and the delicate balance and interactions of multitude of factors, e.g. temperature, eutrophication, predominant phytoplankton taxa, and many more, present a field of unexplored research directions especially when the role of trace metals is considered. It is towards this specific knowledge gap where we intend to contribute in by focusing on the interactive effects of iron and nickel availability with nitrate concentration and how the interdependence of these factors dictate the growth and toxin production of two model HAB species namely Pyrodinium bahamense and Alexandrium minutum.

column4: Management Effectiveness and Impact of the Locally Managed Marine Protected Areas in Zamboanga Peninsula: Basis for Management Enhancement and Policy Recommendations
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6:
Marine Protected Areas in the Philippines are primarily important in conserving the country's marine biodiversity. It is necessary to determine their status to identify interventions that could be recommended to enhance their effective management further. This proposal will empirically assess the management effectiveness and impact of the locally managed marine protected areas in the Zamboanga Peninsula for enhancement and policy recommendations. 

This study will be conducted among the five locally managed MPAs in Zamboanga Peninsula. These MPAs were chosen from different provinces based on size, particularly those with the biggest core area. The Management Effectiveness Tracking Tool (METT) 4 will be utilized to evaluate the management effectiveness of the MPAs. Biophysical assessments will be conducted to assess the impact of the locally managed marine protected areas on the marine ecosystem. Likewise, surveys will be conducted to assess the level of awareness and support of the stakeholders to the MPAs.            By assessing the management effectiveness of the MPAs being implemented by different Local Government Units, the study can develop a range of management effectiveness, where the highest performing LGU will serve as a benchmark in improving the management of other MPAs.

column4: Applying coastal observation and modeling systems to address. Project 1. Applying coastal observation and modeling systems to address different use cases in Philippine coastal waters
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: The marine and coastal waters of the Philippines are experiencing multiple threats as coastal development, pollution, harmful algal blooms and climate change impact them. These lead to compromised conditions of these waters and the ecosystems situated within, which redound to the difficulty of sustaining the resources Filipinos rely on. Despite these risks to ocean resources, key properties of coastal waters are not consistently and transparently tracked, changes are not well-understood and attributed, and there is no capacity to evaluate different scenarios and plan for the long-term based on projected changes. This project aims to fill in an important gap and develop the capacity for consistent, rapid and high frequency ocean observation, and for ocean physical and biogeochemical/ecological modeling. Data and information from these observation and modeling systems will then be applied to a variety of use cases in the target sites. Inherent in this process in the engagement with stakeholders to come up with a co-designed fit-for-purpose ocean observation and modeling system. This project builds on and expands the outputs from previous programs that have begun local development of sensors and informatics systems.

One best example is the fry counting operations of milkfish hatcheries, to which until now, uses manual methods in its operations. Philippines having a 2.5 billion milkfish fry produced, to which all of these were counted manually, only shows the tedious and inefficient hatchery operations and technology that the Philippine Milkfish Industry currently have. With that said, the proposed project aims to provide new technology to answer the current problem on manual counting of milkfish fry to elevate the current hatchery methods into a more efficient and productive processes.

column4: Development of qPCR Assay for the Detection and Quantification of Harmful Kareniacean Dinoflagellates in Selected Coastal Waters of Central Luzon
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6:
As part of the priority projects under the Natural Resources and Environment R&D Agent of Updated Harmonized National Research and Development Agenda in Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources (2022–2028) of DOST-PCAARRD, the proposed project will provide valuable information in support to the Biodiversity R&D program which will specifically focus the genetic diversity and temporal abundance of kareniacean dinoflagellates in marine ecosystem using qPCR assay.

This study aims to establish a high-resolution method to look into the diversity and quantification of the kareniacean dinoflagellates in the three main coastal areas of Central Luzon which will assist the country’s monitoring program and fish-farming operators. With the effective and efficient molecular method, BFAR will efficiently monitor and understand the occurrence of harmful kareniacean dinoflagellate and issue early warnings to local stakeholders to decrease the loss of aquaculture industries during the HAB events.

In line with the government plan, the outcome of this study will contribute in ensuring food security to effectively manage and mitigate potential losses and health problems due to the red tide of kareniacean dinoflagellates.

column4: Application of the Single-laboratory Validated Radio-Receptor Assay to Support Environmental Risk Assessment (ERA) on Ciguatera Poisoning
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development
column6: Ciguatera Poisoning (CP) is a major risk from the consumption several species of tropical fish. This ignored disease represents a serious problem for community health, tourism and fishing industries in countries with tropical reef ecosystems. It is an increasing problem that exacerbated by degradation of coral reef ecosystems (Darius et al, 2007). CP in the Philippines and worldwide is characterized by limited knowledge of the biology of microalgal species causing toxic outbreaks (mainly Gambierdiscus spp), their toxin production, their distribution and their uptake plus toxin metabolism by fish species. Other negative factors are the lack of recognition of CFP, epidemiological studies, adequate specific treatments, low public awareness and poor capabilities for predicting the toxicity of fish production areas or measuring toxin levels in harvested fish (Chinain et al, 2010). In this proposed project, the Receptor Binding Assay technology established during the previous projects will be applied further for the analysis of other marine biotoxins. An RBA based assay for CP will be designed for the country to have capabilities to analyze CFP levels in seafoods.

column4: Multispectral Unit for Land Assessment (MULA) Satellite Development Localization Project
column6:
The MULA Satellite Development Localization Project is the next phase in the Philippines’ spacecraft roadmap for developing commercial-grade satellites. This project builds on the achievements of the MULA Satellite Development Project which is currently being developed in partnership with a UK-based company. 

MULA's contract comes with a license to rebuild, customize, and manufacture a similar satellite in-country. Rebuilding MULA-class satellites opens opportunities for increasing domestically sourced or developed components and subsystems, towards building and strengthening a local industrial base for the country to take a slice of the growing new space economy. The country stands to reap the benefits of gaining more self-reliance and sufficiency by strengthening our space capabilities domestically.

The MULA Satellite Development Localization Project will include the design and development of a MULA-class satellite, with a target of at least 20% of its modules and subsystems developed or procured locally , such as but not limited to the following components:
(1)	Magnetorquer
(2)	GPS Antenna
(3)	High Pressure Tanks for propulsion
(4)	Propulsion Tank support structure
(5)	Fill and vent valves

Furthermore, the project will establish a dedicated Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) Facility to support the complete integration and validation of space systems, ranging from CubeSats (Maya-class) to small satellites of up to approximately 200 kg (MULA-class). The AIT Facility will be strategically located within the selected host site in the country, enabling proximity to key research, academic, and industrial partners, and facilitating efficient logistics, collaboration, and personnel access. 

This facility will serve as a critical infrastructure for ensuring that all satellite modules and subsystems—whether locally developed or procured—are properly assembled, functionally integrated, and rigorously tested to meet mission requirements and international standards.

column4: Development of Water Footprint Decision Support & Visualization System for Sustainable Urban Water Management
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Urbanization trends suggest that by 2050, over two-thirds of the global population will live in cities, creating immense strain on urban development, particularly water supply and sanitation systems. Traditional centralized water management approaches with linear consumption patterns are increasingly unsustainable in the face of rapid urban growth and climate change.

Water footprint accounting offers a valuable tool for fostering water-wise urban development. This method helps cities assess and analyze water use across sectors, identifying inefficiencies and areas for improvement. By considering the three components of water footprints—blue water (surface and groundwater), green water (rainwater stored in soil), and grey water (polluted water from production)—cities gain a comprehensive understanding of water consumption.

As urban populations expand, adopting water-wise practices becomes critical. Integrating water footprint accounting into planning enables cities to secure sustainable water resources and contribute to global efforts for water-resilient urban environments.

column4: Sustainable Concrete Construction in the Philippines using Recycled Concrete Aggregates
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Recycled Concrete Aggregate (RCA) offers numerous benefits. It supports sustainable development, reduces CO2 levels by absorbing some emissions, is likely more cost-effective than traditional aggregates, and minimizes the need for new concrete waste landfills (Happhoadmin7, 2021). However, RCA has drawbacks, such as reduced concrete quality due to adhered mortar and potential durability issues. While supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) can improve durability, the lack of standardized specifications and guidelines remains a significant barrier to its widespread adoption in construction.

Despite these challenges, RCA is gaining popularity. Research is ongoing to enhance the strength and durability of concrete containing RCA. Currently, RCA is primarily used in applications like bulk backfill, soil stabilization, landscaping, road bases, and non-structural concrete. Its use in high-strength structural projects is limited, but advancements in research and policy development could soon enable RCA's broader application in residential and building construction.

column4: Pharmaceutical Leads for Cancer from Mindanao Marine Sponges Year 1
column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
This project is part of the Discovery, Development and Delivery of Natural Products (D3NP) Core Program of the Premier Research Institute of Science and Mathematics of MSU-Iligan Institute of Technology with the ultimate aim of discovering pure anticancer drug leads or templates sourced out from marine sponges collected off the coasts of Mindanao. It is aligned with the 8-point agenda of the Philippine government in the field of health care. It is also aligned with the priority areas of the Department of Science and Technology in the area of Drug Discovery and Development. The project is a continuation of the research work of the PRISM's Center for Natural Products and Drug Discovery (CNPDD) for the past 3 years which involved the  search for new anticancer drug leads from marine sponges collected off Mindanao.       

The mechanisms of cancer being investigated are apoptosis, proliferation and migration. In a previous project implemented, one hundred (100) nonpolar and polar extracts were obtained from fifty sponges collected off Iligan Bay (Kalangahan, Lugait and Poblacion, Kauswagan).  These extracts were subjected to anti-proliferative, pro-apoptotic and anti-migration activity screening against colon cancer cell line HCT116 and lung cancer cell line A549. Active extracts underwent fractionation and subsequent activity testing has led to the identification of eight (8) top tier workable samples for further investigation:  sponge extract PK-04NPa with anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic properties; sponge extracts PK-01NPa and KL-07NPd with anti-proliferative and antimigratory properties; the anti-proliferative fractions PK-01NPa, KL-09Pa and KL-15NPa; and the pro-apoptotic fractions KL-08NPa and KL-21NPd. It is thus proposed that these eight (8) identified active sponge samples undergo bioassay-guided purification to obtain anti-migration, anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic compounds. Year 1 will focus on the extracts PK-04NPa, KL-08NPa and KL-21NPd. The bioassays to be used in the purification processes will the primary assays for each cancer hallmark, to conserve the amounts of the samples. The obtained active compounds will then undergo spectroscopic measurements for their structure elucidation as well as pertinent orthogonal assays to validate their activities, with determination of IC50 values, amounts permitting.

column4: Expanding Chemical Space for Hypertension: Design and Synthesis of Polyphenol-Thiocarbazone Molecular Hybrids as Potential Anti-Hypertensive Agents
column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
This project focuses on the development of polyphenol-thiosemicarbazone hybrids as potential antihypertensive agents. Molecular hybrids, combining two or more bioactive pharmacophores, offer a unique approach to drug discovery by targeting multiple mechanisms of action within a single molecule. In this study, we will combine the well-documented cardiovascular benefits of flavonoids with the pharmacological potential of thiosemicarbazones, which have demonstrated efficacy in reducing oxidative stress and inflammation—key contributors to hypertension.

The project will begin with computer-aided drug design (CADD) and high-throughput screening to identify promising flavonoid-thiosemicarbazone hybrids with potential antihypertensive activity. These compounds will be designed to modulate multiple pathways involved in blood pressure regulation, such as endothelial function, vasodilation, and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). The promising candidates will be synthetically prepared via microwave-assisted reaction.

The synthesized hybrids will then undergo in vitro evaluation against particular regulator enzymes that regulate the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system to evaluate their effects on key processes related to hypertension. By targeting multiple pathways in hypertension, these flavonoid-thiosemicarbazone hybrids have the potential to offer a more comprehensive approach to managing high blood pressure.

The project aligns with the 8-point socio-economic agenda of the Philippines by contributing to the development of innovative healthcare solutions, improving public health outcomes, and promoting access to safer, more effective treatments for hypertension. Furthermore, this research addresses United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being) by advancing efforts to address the management and treatment of non-communicable diseases, such as cardiovascular disorders, and enhancing health care innovations for long-term well-being.

column4: Automated DNA barcoding workbench for large scale, high-precision biodiversity research and species identification
column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
Automated DNA Barcoding Workbench supports large-scale, high-precision biodiversity research by increasing the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of species identification efforts. This helps meet growing demands in fields like conservation biology, ecological monitoring, environmental policy and even in forensics and food content identification. Here are key reasons for its importance:

Efficiency and Speed: Automating DNA barcoding minimizes manual labor and accelerates the process of species identification, allowing researchers to process large volumes of samples faster. This is critical in large-scale biodiversity studies or environmental monitoring.

Accuracy and Consistency: Automation reduces the risk of human error that can occur during manual data entry, sequence alignment, or species matching. This ensures that results are more consistent and reliable across studies.

High-Throughput Capability: Automated workbenches can handle high volumes of data, which is essential for projects like global biodiversity assessments, environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring, and food safety, where thousands of samples may need to be processed simultaneously.

Integration of Bioinformatics Tools: Automated systems often come with integrated bioinformatics pipelines for sequence analysis, data quality control, and species identification. This allows researchers to quickly align sequences with reference databases (e.g., GenBank, BOLD) and analyze phylogenetic relationships.

Cost-Effectiveness: By reducing the need for manual intervention and improving throughput, automated systems can lower the overall cost of DNA barcoding projects. This makes it more feasible for institutions with limited resources to engage in high-level biodiversity research.

Application in Conservation and Policy: DNA barcoding has applications in identifying endangered species, controlling illegal wildlife trade, and monitoring ecosystems. An automated system ensures that timely and accurate data is available to inform conservation decisions and policies.

column4: Establishment of the Mindanao Advanced Nanomaterials (MindANao) Shared Research Facility to be housed at the Center for Nanoscience Research at PRISM, MSU-IIT
column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
This project pertains to the establishment of the Mindanao Advanced Nanomaterials (MindANao) Shared Research Facility thru the acquisition of advanced equipment for the conduct of different research activities at the Center for Nanoscience Research, MSU-IIT dedicated for the synthesis and characterization of nanomaterials based on ceramics, polymers and semiconductors. The acquisition of equipment would certainly elevate the quality of our research, enhance our competitiveness and collaborations with industry which could help drive knowledge and technology transfer.

A. Ceramic nanomaterials

Research on ceramic nanomaterials has led to significant advancements in various technological applications, owing to their unique properties at the nano-level. These materials exhibit enhanced mechanical strength, thermal stability, and novel functionalities compared to the bulk ones. They play a role in the development of advanced optoelectronic devices, including light-emitting diodes and photodetectors. Today, nanoceramic catalysts are employed in chemical processes, such as catalytic converters in hydrogen production and environmental remediation. In the biomedical area, they are employed in drug delivery, tissue engineering scaffolds, and diagnostic tools. They can be applied also as ceramic coatings onto surfaces for improved corrosion resistance, wear resistance, and durability. Photocatalysts based on nanoceramics are used for water purification, air purification, and the degradation of organic pollutants. Ongoing researches are being conducted for innovative ceramic nanomaterials used as fuel cells to improve energy storage and conversion efficiency.

The synthesis and characterization of ceramic nanomaterials involve intricate processes and advanced techniques to control the size, structure, and properties of ceramic particles at the nanoscale. Specialized equipment such as for atomic layer deposition, template-assisted method, hydrothermal synthesis, and spin coating deposition of nanoceramics are
essential for precise control of synthesis conditions to tailor the properties for specific applications. This is also necessary to develop new ceramic nanomaterials and to improve the performance of the existing ones to expand the range of their applications which could contribute to advancements in materials science and the development of innovative solutions across various industries.

B. Polymeric nanomaterials

Nanopolymers or polymeric nanomaterials have gained significant attention due to their unique properties primarily because of their reduced size and increased surface area. They are essential materials in the industry sector as they can be used as adhesives, building materials, paper, apparel, fibers, plastics, concrete, liquid crystals, photoresists, and coatings. Various synthesis methods are employed to create nanopolymers, including emulsion polymerization, nanoprecipitation, miniemulsion polymerization, template-assisted methods, and self-assembly. These methods allow for the controlled production of nanoscale polymer structures.

C. Semiconducting nanomaterials

Semiconducting materials are the foundation of modern electronics, enabling the development of advanced technologies that have transformed communication, computing, and energy conversion. The ongoing research in materials science continues to push the boundaries of semiconductor technology, leading to innovations in various fields.

Light emitting electrochemical cells (LEECs) based on semiconducting nanomaterials are promising technologies for display, solid state lighting, and wearable electronics that are low-cost, energy-saving, and environmentally friendly. In the health sector, LEECs can be significant in terms of medical applications, for example, spectroscopy and lab-on-chips technologies to examine and diagnose certain medical conditions. By doing so, LEEC technologies can help the Philippines meet its objective of enhancing access to healthcare and improving the quality of healthcare services. In textile industries, LEEC technologies can be integrated to fibers for wearable electronics. Artificial lighting for indoor agriculture farming can also benefit LEEC technologies as they are energy-efficient. Synthesis of these LEECs can be done via atomic layer deposition (ALD). It is a highly sought-after technique with high conformal coating and precisely controlled thin film deposition. In semiconductor manufacturing, selective area coating, especially nano-patterning, can potentially be improved by ALD coating techniques through modification of surface chemistry. The controlled atomic- scale conformal coating of ALD is also currently explored to enhance the efficiency and performance of photovoltaics and displays that is highly affected by the quality of interfaces among different layers which influence carrier transportation for electron-hole generation and recombination.

column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
One dragging impetus with advancing industrialization is high waste generation. The Environmental Management Bureau of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources  releases an annual report on the Philippines’ solid waste management status. From its 2015 report, it is projected that from 14.66 million metric tons of waste generated in 2014, the country will produce 20.5 million metric tons of solid wastes by the year 2030. Additional quantification from the Senate Economic Planning Office (SEPO) further reports that the country’s daily waste generation from 37,427.46 tons per day in 2012 steadily increased to 40,087.45 tons in 2016. From this data, the country will yield a 165-percent increase to 77,776 tons of accumulated daily waste by 2025. Synonymously, modernization equates to extremely high energy consumption. This interaction sets the stage for a focal nexus in societal sustainability. The Philippines being restricted by the Clean Air Act of 1999 (RA 8749) prohibits incineration as a waste management option. As a result, the quest for alternative waste management strategies is crucial. 

Solid Waste Management is one of the major challenges that most urban and even rural areas are facing. Current waste management facilities like landfills cannot accommodate the exponential growth in solid waste generation. Iligan City, for one, has a waste generation of approximately 250 tons/day and with a lone central material recovery facility (CMRF) in Brgy. Bonbonon with currently halted activities due to unregulated operations and nearing threshold capacity. Local barangays were tasked to handle their own waste management responsibilities by encouraging household segregation systems and installing Materials Recovery Facilities (MRF) in their barangays but even these cannot keep up with the accumulation of residual solid wastes.

Sultan Naga Dimaporo (SND) is a municipality in the southern part of the region which utilizes 92% of its land area for agriculture. According to PSA, SND belongs to the third-class economy which means quality of life has a huge void to be narrowed. A technological way to improve livelihood while augmenting yield productivity such as easy access to electricity in remote areas would be beneficial to the local residents.

Hence, the need to adapt to waste-to-energy (WTE) technologies like gasification. 

The United Nations has set 17 interconnected global goals which were designated as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SGDs). This project is in line with four of the seventeen SGDs:
SDG 7 - Affordable and Clean Energy
The project aims to provide access to green and renewable energy by converting waste to fuel and ultimately, to energy to be utilized by communities, especially in remote areas
SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities
The project intends to achieve sustainable communities by utilizing waste materials to be used as fuel for power generation
SDG 12 - Responsible Consumption and Production
The project intends to advocate for responsible consumption and production by promoting waste reduction and management practices 
SDG 13 - Climate Action
The project intends to contribute to the global collaboration on climate action by transitioning to renewable energy sources with lower gas emissions

The adaptation of this WTE technology holds the vision to power up semi-remote communities in an environmentally-safe way while harnessing the communities’ generated unwanted wastes.

The Dynamic Mechanical Analyzer (DMA) is a technique such that a small deformation is applied to a sample in a cyclic manner. This allows the material's response to stress, temperature, frequency and other parameters to be studied. column4: Q-RIEnTe Project: Quantum Computing-Based Forecasting and Optimization Applied to Electric Power Grid
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Quantum computing, though still in its early stages, holds immense potential to revolutionize algorithm efficiency. However, its practical applications remain largely untapped in the Philippines, particularly in academia, businesses, and the energy sector. Hybrid-quantum computing, which combines the strengths of classical and quantum systems, has emerged as a promising paradigm to accelerate the adoption of quantum technologies.

To address the gap in awareness and viability of quantum computing in the Philippines, particularly in the energy industry, this project proposes a proof of concept to demonstrate the practical application of hybrid-quantum computing for predictive and prescriptive analytics in power engineering. Specifically, the project will develop hybrid-quantum models for forecasting electricity demand, wind speed, solar irradiance, and electricity prices. Additionally, it will implement hybrid-quantum unit commitment models to support decision-making and hypothesis testing, particularly in evaluating the feasibility of diversifying renewable energy sources at BATELEC I.

The project also aims to consolidate its findings into a position paper that underscores the viability and benefits of hybrid-quantum computing analytics. This paper will serve as a tool to raise awareness and advocate for the adoption of quantum technologies among industries, academia, and government agencies in the Philippines, paving the way for future innovation and collaboration.

column4: PREEMPT, PREDICT, AND TREAT GTD (PREDICTION, EVALUATION, AND TREATMENT OF GESTATIONAL TROPHOBLASTIC DISEASES [GTD OR HMOLE AND ITS CANCER] AMONG FILIPINO WOMEN): Project 1. Preempt GTN (Predicting and Evaluating Molar Pregnancy Transformation to Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia)
column6: Hydatidiform mole is a type of gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) that has potential for malignant transformation (persistent trophoblastic disease or PTD) to invasive mole or choriocarcinoma. Prophylactic chemotherapy is given for at-risk groups based on identified clinical criteria, as followed by PGH, but studies have shown inconsistent results on its benefits, and the clinical factors cannot precisely identify cases that potentially become malignant. The Project 1 aims to determine clinical, ultrasound parameters and genetic profiles that predict development of PTD. This project will establish additional parameters (ultrasound and genetic profile) other than clinical factors that will have clinical utility in the evaluation and management of GTD. It aims to provide more recent local data, and aid in the establishment of additional parameters for early diagnosis and management programs of Filipinos with GTD using advances in genomics and molecular biology. Results of this study are important in providing research-based data as a basis to improve policies and preventive program for gestational trophoblastic disease in the Philippines.

column6:
Bananas are a valuable fruit crop and a key part of global agriculture, but increased production has led to significant by-products and waste, such as banana blossoms. These blossoms, despite their low market value due to inconsistent demand, are rich in nutrients and bioactive compounds like antioxidants, phenolics, proteins, and dietary fibers, highlighting their potential health benefits. Utilizing banana blossoms to create new products offers a sustainable way to reduce agricultural waste and add value.

This study aims to develop an optimized banana blossom powder as a versatile food ingredient. The powder will be packaged as a ready-to-commercialize product and tested in a prototype like Pandesal. By transforming banana by-products into valuable ingredients, this initiative can provide environmental, social, and economic benefits. It supports food security, stimulates economic growth, and creates new opportunities in agriculture and related industries.

column4: Prototyping and Technical Evaluation of a Customized Turtle Excluder Device (ProTECTED)
column5: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column6:
Turtle fishing was banned in the Philippines in the 1980s and also in other countries since the 1970s.  Although fishermen have not been conducting turtle fishing, the number of turtles is still decreasing due to unintended catching of them. Most of the turtle are being caught in shrimp trawl nets. To avoid this, the National Marine Fisheries Services (NMFS) of the USA develop a Turtle Excluder Device (TED) to reduce the incidental capture of the endangered sea turtle by shrimp trawls since the 1980s. The US also implemented a policy to ban the imports of shrimp’s countries without TED application similar to the US methods.

In 1996, the United States Embassy in Manila informed the Philippine government that the United States will embargo shrimps trawled in open water in the countries without sea turtle protection program beginning May 1, 1996. With the presence of marine sea turtles in the country, the Philippines is one of the countries where export is embargoed. 

In 2010, the Philippines also implemented a regulation on the use of TED, not just in the shrimp industry but for the whole trawl fishing industry. But for several years, the industry has not been following the regulation. The Philippines is a net exporter of shrimp, which contributed 25% to total fish and fisheries exports. Strict implementation of the US Embargo would greatly affect not just the fishermen, but also the economy.

This proposed study aims to develop a TED design that is comparable to the design of NMFS and qualify to the US requirement to be able to lift the embargo. The study will create a design in consideration with the local sea environment, size of trawl nets and size of boats used. Furthermore, the study will also optimize the design not to affect the catching efficiency of shrimp and to achieve higher turtle releasing efficiency.

column4: UPLB Alt TAMIS Program: Development of Microbial-based Alternative Sweetener from Sugarcane Bagasse
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
This program focuses on transforming sugarcane bagasse (SB), a low-value by-product of sugar production, into low-calorie, functional sweeteners like xylitol and mannitol. This approach addresses environmental waste and sugar-related health issues, such as diabetes, obesity, and dental problems, by providing natural, health-friendly alternatives to traditional sweeteners.

Microbial production of sugar alcohols from SB offers a sustainable and cost-effective method with minimal environmental impact. Xylitol and mannitol, derived via fermentation, are bio-organic and highly sought after in the pharmaceutical and food industries due to their sweetening power, anti-carcinogenic properties, and suitability for diabetic and dental products. The xylitol market, valued at $700M in 2023, is projected to grow significantly in the coming decade.

The program aims to optimize SB pre-treatment techniques, such as ultrasound-assisted hydrolysis, to reduce production costs and environmental pollutants. It will also explore microbial fermentation and enzyme immobilization to enhance the efficiency and yield of xylitol and mannitol production. These advancements could pave the way for sustainable, large-scale manufacturing while meeting the growing demand for healthier sweeteners.

Key features of the application include real-time updates on tropical cyclones, specifically their location, track, strength, and impacts. One particularly significant feature is its ability to display the distance of the tropical cyclone from the user's location and assess their degree of exposure at any given time.

column4: Valorization of Virgin Coconut Oil (VCO) Wet Processing Wastes into Coconut Protein Concentrate and Dietary Fiber for Plant-Based Food Products
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
The Philippine virgin coconut oil (VCO) industry is a significant manufacturing sector, generating $92 million from exports in 2022. With a projected annual growth rate of 7.35% in the global VCO market, the implementation of the Philippine Coconut Industry Roadmap (2021-2024), and the enactment of the Coconut Farmer and Industry Fund Act, VCO production is expected to increase. Additionally, growing awareness of VCO’s health benefits, including its potential as a COVID-19 treatment, is driving higher demand.

This anticipated rise in VCO production will result in increased waste generation, including coconut skim milk and coconut residue, which constitute approximately 63% of coconut meat. For every kilogram of VCO produced, nearly one kilogram each of skim milk and residue is generated, often discarded, used as animal feed, or upcycled on a small scale. These by-products, rich in proteins (skim milk) and dietary fiber (residue), hold potential as plant-based ingredients.

This study aims to valorize these wet processing wastes by developing coconut protein concentrates (CPC) and coconut dietary fiber (CDF) for use in plant-based milk and meat alternatives, promoting sustainability and adding value to the VCO production process.

column4: PROGRAM TO SUPPORT THE INITIATIVES ON INBORN ERRORS OF METABOLISM FOR THE BETTER STATE OF HEALTH (SIBS PROGRAM): Project 1: An Evaluation of Nutritional Status, Body Composition, and Dietary Intakes of Filipino Pediatric Patients with Inborn Errors of Intermediary Protein Metabolism
column6: Inborn errors of Intermediary Protein Metabolism (IEIPM) are rare genetic and inherited disorders due to a defect in enzymes, cofactors, or transporters in metabolic pathways that interfere with the normal metabolism of amino acids leading to the accumulation of toxic substances. In the Philippines, IEIPM belonged to the most common inherited metabolic disease and these include Amino Acid Disorders, Branched Chain Organic Acidemias, and Urea Cycle Defects. Pediatric patients with IEIPM require a lifelong dietary treatment that necessitates restriction to proper amounts of natural protein in the diet complemented with medical food and supplements for metabolic control and stability, and to promote a better state of health. However, following the most restrictive diets may potentially expose patients to nutritional risks and is most likely to influence long-term nutritional status, body composition, and growth patterns. Several researches have been done to examine the nutritional characteristics of children with IEIPM who are receiving regular active medical and dietary treatment and its implications for their state of health. However, there is a scarcity of studies conducted among Filipinos in specific. This study intends to evaluate the nutritional status, growth, body composition, dietary intake, selected biochemical and clinical profile of Filipino pediatric patients diagnosed with IEIPM. A well-evaluated nutritional characteristic of Filipino Pediatric Patients with IEIPM will aid researchers, clinicians, and policymakers to provide a more fitting reference for nutrition management guidelines in the Philippines.

column6:

column4: SEVEN LAKES ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING PROGRAM: STRATEGIES TOWARD SUSTAINABLE LAKE ECOSYSTEM (7 LAMPS) - PHASE 2: Project 3. Development of Accessible Detection Methods for Improved Monitoring of Waterborne Pathogens in Environmental Waters
column6: Crysptosporidium and Giardia are protozoan parasites which have been implicated in numerous waterborne outbreaks of diarrheal disease. Molecular epidemiological research on Cryptosporidium and Giardia have revealed strong host specificity and zoonotic transmission, thus making them good candidates for source tracking of fecal contamination in environmental waters. However, detection of these parasites in the environment has not been considered in regular monitoring efforts due to cost and technical manpower requirements. This study aims to assess the use of waterborne parasitic protozoans, specifically Cryptosporidium and Giardia, as sentinels for waterborne pathogen monitoring in Sampaloc, Bunot, and Calibato Lakes, San Pablo City, and to develop a prototype of a portable fluorescent photometer set-up for real-time detection of Cryptosporidium sp. in environmental waters.

column4: Identification of Multi-Omics Profiles Affecting Care and Treatment of Colorectal Cancer in the Philippines (IMPACT – CRC)
column6: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most diagnosed cancer and the fourth-leading cause of cancer deaths in the country, with a younger mean age at diagnosis compared to Western populations. As CRC in the Philippines has a distinct etiology compared to that in Western societies, this study will characterize the gut microbiome, metabolome, and miRNome profile in Filipinos diagnosed with CRC and link this information to cancer development and patient outcome. It will provide novel information relevant to CRC globally and specific information pertinent to Filipino patients. Our study findings aim to elucidate novel mechanisms of CRC development using multi-omics approaches based on the information on viral and bacterial agents present in colorectal tissue and fecal samples, together with knowledge of the miRNome, will inform on strategies for disease treatment and prevention, such as targeting miRNAs and manipulation of the gut microbiome to affect disease outcomes.

column4: Machine Learning of Physics-based Earthquake-Induced Landslide Parameters and for Efficient Prediction and Warning in the Philippines
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: This project compares two approaches in Modelling Earthquake Induced landslides. First is utilizing Physics-Enhanced Machine Learning (PEML) that combines existing measurements of data with underlying physical models, when they are available, to refine soil and seismic parameters essential for landslide modeling. This includes using Newmark’s equation for deterministic landslide modeling and incorporating remote sensing and AI-based image classification to automate and validate landslide inventories. Second is a new SEM-Newmark displacement method is employed to simulate three-dimensional wave fields, enhancing the accuracy of regional seismic induced landslide assessments.

column4: THE DOST ST&I FORESIGHT DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM: Project 1. Development of the PAGTANAW 2050, the Philippine ST&I Foresight Indicators
column6:
In the Philippines, indicators for science, technology, and innovation (ST&I) are lacking or
insufficient. The PAGTANAW 2050 is the country’s first foresight document focused on ST&I that provides a compendium of ST&I megatrends revolving around PAGTANAW 2050’s 12 Key Operational Areas (KOAs).

ST&I indicators provide the widely acknowledged function of monitoring the performance of institutions in countries or nations in terms of science, technology, and innovation. This suggests that these players are continuously being benchmarked, or at the very least compared, in the ST&I dimension. As a result, identifying and interpreting indicators requires a clear understanding of the fundamental processes that underpin science, technology, and innovation.

Through a series of workshops, the consolidated indicators will be collated and later prioritized by experts to create a unified list of indicators. The identified and prioritized indicators for the twelve (12) KOAs and four (4) clusters will serve as the baseline data for monitoring and evaluation of the emerging trends and technologies encompassing ST&I in the country.

column4: PiliXtractify: Improvement of Pili-Pulp Oil Extraction Method Through Automation and Smart Technologies
column6: The Bicol Region dominates Pili production in the Philippines, with 90% of the cultivation area and 84% of the total output. The Pili fruit has three parts: the pulp, the shell, and the kernel. The more useful part of the fruit is the large kernel because it is rich in oil, which is valued for its quality. Despite being discarded, the pulp, approximately 64% of the fruit weight, contains oil and other valuable bioactive compounds. Demand for Pili pulp oil is rising among cosmetic and wellness industries locally and abroad. Presently, manual extraction methods limit yield and quality consistency. Mechanization and automation offer a solution that reduces contamination risks and enables efficient, high-quality Pili pulp oil production. This approach addresses current limitations, aiming for enhanced productivity and commercialization of top-grade Pili products.

column4: Development of Cost-Effective Wastewater Treatment Systems for Local Government Units in the Province of Bulacan to Facilitate Compliance to the Supreme Court Continuing Mandamus Order on Manila Bay
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Wastewater management in Bulacan faces significant challenges, including industrial pollution, inadequate municipal treatment facilities, and non-compliance with environmental regulations. Many industries lack efficient wastewater treatment systems, leading to discharges that fail to meet standards and pollute local water resources. Municipal facilities are also insufficient, with only Baliwag and San Jose Del Monte operating septage treatment plants, which cannot serve all 24 municipalities. Pulilan has sought assistance in addressing these issues, prompting NWSteel Technologies Inc. to establish a septage treatment facility to serve Pulilan and nearby areas. The lack of real-time testing facilities further hinders effective monitoring and compliance with water quality standards.

In collaboration with NWSteel Technologies, which has expertise in wastewater treatment, ITDI proposes establishing a modular, scalable facility in Bulacan to serve as a research and innovation hub. This facility will develop customized solutions for local wastewater challenges, promoting the adoption of advanced and locally-developed water treatment technologies. Using Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) technology, the facility aims to initially treat domestic wastewater from Bulacan's 20 municipalities and 4 component cities, with potential future use in the province's 209 food processing facilities.

column4: Upgrading of facilities and expansion of metals and engineering innovation center in The National Capital Region (MEIC – NCR) and Regions VI and VII
column5: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column6:
The Department of Science and Technology, through the Metals Industry Research and Development Center (MIRDC) in cooperation with SUCs and DOST Regional Offices  established state-of-the-art facilities that seek to spur R&D activities and provide readily access to experts/consultants, and services on metal and equipment fabrication needed by local MSMEs to increase their productivity and competitive advantage through the projects, “Establishment of Metals & Engineering Innovation Centers (MEIC) in CAR, Regions I, II, III and X” (or MEIC Batch 1) and “Establishment of Metals & Engineering Innovation Centers (MEIC) in Regions IV-A, IV-B, V, VI, VII, VII, IX, XI, XII, and Caraga” (or MEIC Batch 2).

However, Republic Act No. 12000, also known as the ""Negros Island Region Act,"" which was passed into law on 11 June 2024.  This mandated the establishment of the Negros Island Region (NIR or Region XVIII). The region comprises the provinces of Negros Occidental, including the City of Bacolod, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor, along with their respective cities, municipalities, and barangays.  The MEICs under the MEICB2 project were established in Technological University of the Philippines – Visayas (TUP-V), in Talisay City, Negros Occidental and the Negros Oriental State University (NorSU), in Dumaguete City, Negros Oriental, for Regions VI and VII, respectively.  With the said creation of NIR, this placed both regions without their own MEIC and defeated the original intent of DOST and MIRDC to expand services in all regions.

Further for the last 5 years, the MIRDC which served as the MEIC in the National Capital Region (NCR), was left with the existing machines and equipment below par on the facilities of the newly established MEICs in the regions. Likewise, the location of the MIRDC is quite difficult to reach by some of the firms in the NCR who would like to collaborate and partner for the development of new products or services. 

To further strengthen the metalworking and prototyping capabilities, and human resource (faculties and researchers) development to advance Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) in the NCR, the acquisition of new state-of-the-art equipment, training of researchers in the various advanced technologies, and establishment of new extension facilities of MEIC-NCR.  These long-term investments in building the local capacity for technology generation can lead to innovations that will give firms a competitive advantage. This can result in the creation of new firms and even entirely new industries that can provide high-quality jobs.

column4: Development of Forecasting Tool on the Impact of Population Dynamics on National and Local Development
column6:
Population dynamics - covering demographic processes such as fertility, mortality, and migration - are central to shaping the Philippines’ path toward sustainable national and local development. With a population exceeding 112 million and a youthful demographic profile with 34.7% of said figure belonging to 15-34 years old,  the country stands at a critical point, which if not maximized, can lose our chance to reap its possible economic benefits. 

Declining fertility rates and rising life expectancy signal a demographic transition that could yield a demographic dividend, where a larger share of the population is of working age and able to drive economic growth. At the same time, rapid urbanization places mounting pressure on infrastructure, housing, and public services; while migration patterns, including the significant role of Overseas Filipino Workers, continue to influence the country’s economic and labor environment.

These demographic shifts carry profound implications for development planning. A youthful population demands expanded access to quality education and employment opportunities to fully harness its potential, while an aging population requires responsive health systems to address non-communicable diseases and long-term care. Local governments face uneven challenges, with some regions struggling with overcrowding and resource strain, while others contend with depopulation and economic stagnation. Population trends also directly affect progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals, influencing poverty reduction, gender equality, and environmental sustainability.

Despite these realities, policy makers, planners and program implementers often lack accessible tools to forecast and assess how population dynamics will affect long-term development. Planning is hindered by fragmented data and limited integration of demographic trends with economic and social indicators, leaving policies vulnerable to gaps in foresight. To address this, the project seeks to develop a forecasting tool that can simulate scenarios like fertility decline, migration shifts, or urban expansion, and provide evidence-based insights to guide both national strategies and local governance. 

Aligning with the CPD Philippine Population and Development Plan of Action (PPD-POA), the development of a forecasting tool tailored to the Philippine context would strengthen evidence-based policies and programs, ensuring that population dynamics are harnessed as drivers of inclusive growth and sustainable development rather than sources of vulnerability.

column4: BRIDGING THE GAP ON COFFEE PRODUCTION AND PROCESSINNG THROUGH EMERGING RESEARCH AND INNOVATION FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF THE INDUSTRY (CvSU BEAN PROGRAM): Project 3. From Cherries to Cup: Microbiological, Metabolomic, and Sensory Profiling of Liberica Coffee
column6: Coffee is an important beverage that makes significant impact on Philippine economy and society. The postharvest management operations critically play important role in coffee quality production. The coffee quality is primarily associated with postharvest management operations, which include the wet fermentation method. Fermentation is a crucial process and primarily driven by endogenous microorganisms that simply facilitate the degradation of coffee cherries mucilage, thereby affecting the quality of green coffee bean (GCB) and coffee brew. Among the types of coffee produced in the country, Liberica coffee (Coffea liberica) is known to have a poor cup quality and extensive studies must be done to determine the factors affecting the cup quality and how to improve its quality and production. Molecular approach (e.g., next generation sequencing) in determining the taxonomic microbiome profile and abundance patterns during fermentation is essential to evaluate which group of microorganisms is increased or decreased during the process. Beneficial microbes can be targeted and cultivated to be used as starter cultures. In addition, metabolomic analysis approaches will determine which volatile organic compounds are present during fermentation and in the GCB of Liberica coffee. The identity of these compounds will provide us basis on how to modify, improve, and optimize the process to produce high quality of GCB metabolite profile over time. The microbiome and metabolomic profiles obtained from different fermentation periods will be correlated with the green coffee bean and cup quality of Liberica coffee roasted beans, which will provide a baseline data on the associated factors in fermentation that affect the GCB and cup quality of Liberica coffee. The basic information generated by the project can serve as a basis of determining the beneficial microbes and metabolites that contribute to the flavor and taste of coffee as well as detrimental microbes and metabolites that produce off flavor to coffee. This project will soon provide assistance to the smallholder women and men coffee farmers and processors on how to possibly improve the quality of Liberica coffee, by modifying the fermentation process.

Cagayan de Oro City (CDOC) faces a pressing challenge as municipal solid waste (MSW) generation is projected to double by 2045. Legislative efforts, such as Senate Bill 2267, promote waste-to-energy (WtE) technologies to address this issue, but implementation faces hurdles, including technical, economic, and environmental concerns, particularly regarding emissions.

To overcome these challenges, we propose a decision support system (DSS) that combines MSWtE process modeling, machine learning (ML), and multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM). This system will provide data-driven insights for selecting and deploying MSWtE technologies while optimizing infrastructure placement, reducing environmental impact, and improving energy efficiency. The DSS will involve key stakeholders, including government units, policymakers, urban planners, energy providers, and communities, ensuring comprehensive and sustainable solutions.

Our approach leverages MSWtE technologies alongside smart city principles to guide CDOC toward sustainable waste management. By turning waste into a resource, the initiative addresses environmental, economic, and social challenges, contributing to CDOC’s transformation into a smart and sustainable city.

column4: Support for the PH Gaming Industry Towards Embracing In-House Game Engine Development
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
In the Philippine gaming industry, most 2D or 3D games for PC, mobile, AR, or VR are developed using proprietary game engines like Unity or Unreal. While convenient, this approach has drawbacks. These engines often require revenue-sharing once games achieve significant commercial success. Technically, developers lack full control over the engine's architecture, limiting innovation in low-level mechanics and graphics techniques. Additionally, games built with these engines tend to have larger file sizes and slower performance due to the inclusion of the engine's runtime environment. Developers in the Philippines have limited options beyond Unity, Unreal, or Godot.

To overcome these limitations and align with practices of Western and European companies creating groundbreaking AAA games, we propose developing a framework for customized in-house game engines. This approach utilizes open-source alternatives, leveraging low-level graphics APIs like DirectX or OpenGL and C++ for core components. The framework builds on materials from the proponents' undergraduate game engine architecture course, providing a foundation for empowering local developers with greater control and innovation opportunities.

Technological advancements, particularly gamification, offer innovative solutions for revitalizing TSG in the digital age. Gamifying TSG allows for the interactive teaching of rules, techniques, and play styles, making them more engaging and accessible. Incorporating AI tools enhances this experience by tailoring gameplay to individual skill levels and providing deeper insights into player engagement and cultural significance through advanced analytics.

This project focuses on gamifying the traditional sports and games of the Cordillera Administrative Region to achieve two key goals: preserving cultural heritage and creating a unique, interactive learning platform. By digitizing and sharing TSG knowledge, rules, and mechanics, the project ensures these traditions endure and remain accessible to future generations.

column4: NEPHCO (NEutron PHoton COnverter): A Compact, Multilayered Neutron-to-Photon Converter for Long-Term, Sustainable High-Energy Gamma-Rays
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: This study outlines the development of the NEPHCO (NEutron PHoton COnverter) system, a solution to address the current lack in the Philippines of a sustainable, cost-efficient, high-energy photon source capable of delivering a range of distinct photon energies beyond 3 MeV. Once realized, this photon source is expected to open new avenues for various industrial materials analysis applications, such as Prompt Gamma Neutron Activation Analysis (PGNAA). It will enable the accurate calibration of radiation detectors, bolster the reliability of national dosimetry in the high-energy photon ranges in medical accelerator and nuclear facilities, and broaden national educational capacity in nuclear, high-energy photon, and space radiation sciences and technologies. The focus of NEPHCO is to maximize the use of an existing 241Am-Be neutron source at the DOST-PNRI, a valuable asset with a half-life of 432.2 years. NEPHCO aims to augment this source by introducing an optimized system that converts these neutrons into high-energy photons through the process of thermal neutron capture, a type of nuclear reaction. The project aspires to align with national S&T priorities, enhancing sectors from nuclear, photonic, and space radiation research to national radiation dosimetric capacity and industrial material analysis. It has four main objectives: (1) to design, optimize, and construct the NEPHCO; (2) to integrate NEPHCO into the lab, enhancing radiation field characteristics and safety; (3) to apply NEPHCO for high-energy photon spectrometry and dosimetry R&D; and (4) to utilize NEPHCO to foster and promote nuclear and high-energy radiation education.

column4: SWIFT: Sustainable Wheels with Innovative Metamaterials for Future Transportation
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: Land transportation is essential for modern society, facilitating travel and goods transport, but pneumatic tires, commonly used in the sector, have limitations such as punctures, high maintenance, and reduced suitability for diverse terrains. This project proposes the development of airless, non-pneumatic tires made from sustainable metamaterials, offering superior durability, strength, lightweight properties, and puncture resistance. These tires aim to reduce downtime, maintenance, and fuel consumption, enhancing productivity and cost efficiency, particularly in rural areas with rough roads. Partnering with DOST-MIRDC and AMCEN, the project will focus on designing scalable manufacturing processes to ensure affordability and market readiness. By integrating sustainable airless tires, the transportation sector can benefit from improved safety, reduced environmental impact, and increased fuel efficiency while creating new job opportunities and fostering innovation.

column4: Design and Development of Additively Manufactured Polymer Based Liquid Cooling System for Enhancing Thermal Performance of Double-side Cooled Power Modules for Electric Vehicles Application (AMPoLiCoolS)
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: The increasing demand for Electronic Vehicle applications necessitates the development of efficient thermal management solutions to ensure the optimal performance and longevity of power modules. In particular, the transition towards double-sided cooling configurations presents challenges in dissipating heat effectively from both sides of the modules. Current cooling manifolds employed for thermal management often lack lightweight design, leading to increased vehicle weight and decreased energy efficiency. Thus, there is a critical need to develop a lightweight cooling manifold tailored for double-sided cooled power modules in EV applications, capable of efficiently dissipating heat while minimizing additional weight and maximizing energy efficiency.

column4: Accelerating Local Commercial Plant-based, Low-Moisture Extrudate Processing using Rapid Prototyping for Highly-customized Machine Parts and Peripherals through Metal Additive Manufacturing (ACER)
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: Through the Project, the Additive Manufacturing Center (AMCen) will assist the industry partner related to the utilization of metal 3D printing technology (Direct Metal Laser Sintering powder bed fusion(DMLS)/Direct Energy Deposition(DED)/ Metal Binder Jetting(MBJ))  to address the cost and time inefficiencies in extruder machine parts prototyping encountered when using the traditional Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining. The FoodFlow will be responsible for the conduct of production test trials and the assessment of technical quality parameters of the resultant extrudate samples processed using metal 3D printed machine parts relative to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. The Project envisions that a technology package can be transferred to FoodFlow for their utilization to meet the extrudate customization requirements of its clientele. The technology is based on the laboratory-level iterative prototyping phase using metal 3D printing technology to finalize the machine part designs prior to the fabrication of equivalents using CNC for eventual larger scale machineries corresponding to a volume commercial-scale extrudate productions.

column4: Project REMOVE As – Radiation Technology for Efficient Mitigation Of Contaminated Valuable Waters Containing Arsenic
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: In areas where the drinking water contains unsafe levels of arsenic, the immediate concern is finding a safe source of drinking water, and if this cannot be established, the short-term goal is to reduce arsenic levels. The DRR-Team Mission that surveyed and studied the high-arsenic level areas in the Philippines suggested that “it is very likely that treatment based on adsorption or enhanced coagulation, possibly supported by an appropriate pre-treatment will result in more reliable, effective and efficient arsenic removal”. In this proposal, a modified nonwoven fabric will be synthesized and applied as an adsorbent in the removal of arsenic from contaminated water. The iron oxide-coated polypropylene-based adsorbent for arsenic removal will be produced through the radiation-grafting technology. Given the potential merits of the iron oxide-coated fibrous adsorbent produced through radiation-grafting, it is expected to perform better than both the commercial adsorbent and the DRR-Team recommended IHE ADART process. In areas with high arsenic levels, the proposed technology may be easily installed in household water faucets. It may also be installed in the treatment plants of water districts to provide clean and safe water to its customers.

column4: MetalEco: Sustainable Recovery of Valuable Metals from Spent EV Batteries through Continuous Electrochemical System
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: The MetalEco project focuses on sustainable metal recovery from spent electric vehicle (EV) batteries, developing a continuous electrochemical system to extract lithium (Li) and using electrowinning for nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), and manganese (Mn). Recovered metals will be tested for use in lithium coin cells, with a cost-benefit analysis to evaluate feasibility. Outputs include valuable metallic compounds and coin cells with recovered lithium cathodes and carbon nanomaterial anodes from agricultural waste. In partnership with Radicor Metal Manufacturing, the project also seeks to advocate for policies on lithium-ion battery recycling, promoting innovation, sustainability, and a circular economy for electronic waste.

column4: Sustainable Membranes for Aqueous Sodium-Ion Batteries
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
As technology advances, the demand for energy storage grows, with lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) dominating the market for decades. However, LIBs face challenges, including material sourcing, safety risks, and recyclability. Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) offer an alternative, leveraging sodium's abundance and compatibility with existing LIB production lines. Yet, sodium's larger ion size results in lower energy density and reduced ion mobility, limiting SIBs' use in compact, lightweight applications like electronics.

Aqueous sodium-ion batteries (ASIBs) improve safety and affordability with water-based electrolytes but have even lower energy density than SIBs. Despite this, ASIBs are a promising alternative to lead-acid batteries (LABs) in industries where LABs remain standard, offering higher energy density without lead-related environmental concerns. This project aims to enhance ASIB performance by developing advanced membranes and nanomaterials through electrospinning and electrowriting techniques. These innovations will improve separator and electrode efficiency while ensuring scalable, eco-friendly production methods.

column4: Development of Solar-powered Compact Membrane Capacitive Deionization (mCDI) System for Desalination of Brackish Water
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Capacitive deionization (CDI), a cost-effective and energy-efficient desalination technology, has yet to see adoption in the Philippines despite its potential for treating brackish water and freshwater affected by salt intrusion. CDI also offers the unique advantage of partially recovering energy used during ion removal for reuse within the device or for external applications.

This project focuses on advancing CDI by simultaneously developing electrode materials and fabricating a compact membrane CDI (mCDI) module to enhance its readiness for local application, particularly in water-stressed areas. A solar-powered mCDI prototype will be tested for its desalination efficiency and energy recovery capabilities.

The primary goal is to provide an affordable water treatment solution for communities affected by salt intrusion or heavy metal contamination, aligning with the national effort to address water access issues for the 40 million Filipinos lacking formal water supply systems.

column4: TransWOOD: Production of Transparent Wood for Next Generation Smart Building Materials in the Philippines
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: The TransWOOD project aims to investigate the feasibility of producing transparent wood with engineering and architectural applications for smart building materials in the Philippines. Transparent wood is produced by altering the wood’s chemical structure reducing its ability to absorb light followed by impregnating the voids with a clear resin. Transparent wood could potentially be use as replacement for glass windows or for flexible transparent substrate used in many electronic devices, among others. In addition, it is more biodegradable, shatterproof and has excellent insulating properties which make it ideal for smart and energy efficient building material. Unfortunately, no study on transparent wood have been conducted in the Philippines. The TransWOOD project would fabricate transparent wood from low-density, fast growing wood species in the Philippines using methyl methacrylate and polyvinyl acetate resins. The resulting transparent wood will be tested for optical, thermal and mechanical properties to evaluate their suitability to replace glass and for energy efficient smart material. At the successful conclusions of the project, results would be shared with the public through seminars, interviews, journal articles and presentation in scientific conferences. Students and researchers capacitated by the project directly or indirectly will be allowed access to equipment and continuous cooperation from project staff. Sharing of knowledge and best practices in fabricating and testing transparent wood would be encouraged.

column4: COULIGLIG: Cooperative Unified Logistics using Intelligent Grouped Robots
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
The project draws its inspiration from the swarm behavior of cicadas, also known as "Kuliglig" in Tagalog. Cicadas exhibit remarkable coordination and cooperation in their swarming behavior, which serves as a natural model for developing efficient and intelligent group behaviors in robotics, particularly in logistics and coordination tasks. By leveraging principles observed in nature, such as self-organization and collective intelligence, combined with deep reinforcement learning, COULIGLIG aims to create a system of intelligent robots that can work together seamlessly to optimize logistics operations.

Swarm robotics, coupled with deep reinforcement learning, offers a promising approach to enhance the efficiency and adaptability of cobots (collaborative robots) in warehouse and grocery environments. This proposal outlines a comprehensive plan to develop and deploy such cobots, leveraging advanced AI techniques for seamless navigation, task allocation, and optimization.
