column4: Development of a Second Prototype Model Hybrid Electric Train
column5: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column6:
A prototype Hybrid Electric Train (HET) has been successfully designed, developed, and tested by the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) through its research arm, the Metals Industry Research and Development Center (MIRDC). The train consists of one power coach and four rideable coaches, with a maximum capacity of 880 passengers per trip. At 12 meters long, the HET coaches are shorter than typical PNR coaches, earning them the nickname "railbus."

The HET is set to operate as a revenue train on the PNR mainline, serving commuters between Calamba and Alabang Stations after completing its validation testing. This development is a first for the country. Despite the limited railway experience of the MIRDC team and its local fabricator partners, the project is seen as a significant achievement. While an independent assessor identified some gaps between the HET and PNR's existing commercial units, the train passed all required tests, including the RAMS (Reliability, Availability, Maintenance, and Safety) certification.

Throughout the design and testing phases, the MIRDC Trainset Project Team gained valuable knowledge and skills, continuously improving the prototype. These learnings provide a strong foundation for future developments in commercial and commuter train sets.

The PNR General Manager and the DOTr Undersecretary for Railways experienced the HET firsthand on two occasions: June 8 and June 23, 2023. Accompanied by PNR heads and technical consultants, they praised the collaborative efforts of the government and private sectors in creating the HET. Both officials expressed strong support, calling the project a significant step toward sustainable transportation in the country.

A safety workshop involving PNR consultants, PNR personnel, and MIRDC teams highlighted concerns about the dimensions and safety of the prototype. Although the train is operational, additional safety measures and modifications are needed before its commercial deployment. The expertise gained from this project will be instrumental in creating an improved train model.

The HET is the first of its kind in the Philippines. In recognition of its success, the DOTr and PNR plan to collaborate with DOST and MIRDC to develop a second prototype HET focused on cargo operations for commercial use within the PNR system.

column4: Empowering Innovation in Muntinlupa, Taguig, Pateros, Parañaque, and Las Piñas (MUNTAPARLAS): Establishing the Accelerated Science Technology & Innovation Gateway (ASTIG) (DOST-NCR MUNTAPARLAS Satellite Office)

The City Government of Muntinlupa has allocated a 700-square-meter plot of land in Brgy. Sucat to the Department of Science and Technology-National Capital Region (DOST-NCR) through a 50-year Usufruct Agreement. Given that Muntinlupa and the other cities in the MUNTAPARLAS serve as key gateways to the southern part of Luzon, DOST-NCR recognizes this as an opportunity to introduce science and technology-based innovations. This initiative aims to further enhance the business environment in the city and the surrounding areas. 

The DOST-NCR conceptualized the Accelerated Science Technology & Innovation Gateway – ASTIG (with MUNTAPARLAS Clustered Area S&T Office), which will bring in S&T concepts, experts, and outputs from its headquarters in Bicutan, Taguig, onward to Muntinlupa, Pateros, Parañaque and Las Piñas City, aimed at capacitating industries and communities in the Metro’s southern part. 

After the establishment of the DOST-NCR Clustered Area S&T Office in Sucat, Muntinlupa, the ASTIG will funnel S&T initiatives and outputs from the Research and Development Institutions (RDIs) in the DOST Complex to the industrial / business hub in MUNTAPARLAS Cities and municipality. This will also capitalize on the S&T efforts of local universities and colleges in MUNTAPARLAS, including the Colegio De Muntinlupa, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa, Muntinlupa City Technical Institute, Taguig City University, Pateros Technological College, and Parañaque City College. 

An integral part of the Accelerated Science Technology & Innovation Gateway is the new DOST-NCR Clustered Area S&T Office, which will be instrumental in aligning S&T programs of academic institutions in MUNTAPARLAS to the DOST Harmonized National R&D Agenda (HNRDA) and Regional R&D Priority Thrusts.

column4: TECHGROW: Technology Transfer and Entrepreneurship Collaboration and Harmonization of Growing Regional Opportunities on Wealth Creation
column6:
In accordance with the Philippine Technology Transfer Act of 2009 (RA 10055), and DOST Regional Offices' portfolio and technology transfer framework, this project intends to (1) accelerate the DOST Regional Offices (DOST ROs), State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), and Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs)’ innovation capacity for market-driven solutions toward transfer and commercialization of local technologies for inclusive regional development; and (2) identify the R&D needs of communities and industries, evaluate the optimum potential impact per investment made for regional technology transfer activities funded under the Regional Grants-In-Aid Fund, and institutionalize a mechanism for technology reviews to serve as feedback loops from deployment to technology improvements through re-development.
 
In collaboration with DOST Councils, R&D Institutions, and Service Institutions, this project will continuously support the ecosystem of translating R&D to commercialization at the regional level, particularly the SUCs and LUCs that have no access yet to the assistance of DOST Councils. The needs assessment, feedback mechanism, and evaluation of technology transfer initiatives of DOST ROs will align with the DOST Administrative Order 2019-014: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Tool. This will answer the question, “For every peso spent on technology development to transfer, what is the return on investment to the government?” This will also help in addressing the problem of "low adoption of technology".

column4: Innovation for Filipinos Working Distantly from the Philippines (iFWD PH)
column6: The program provides support opportunities for returning Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) and their immediate families by equipping them with the needed skills and expertise to put up their own startup technology-based companies. OFWs under the program undergo two (2) phases, namely: Phase 1 - capability building on technology-based business ideation, technology-based business development and management; and Phase 2 - provision of innovation-enabling funds and continuous assistance through business incubation, technical advisory and consultancy services. column4: Additive Manufacturing Design and Validation Approaches for Novel Conformal Cooling through Advanced Experiments and Simulations in Metal Molding (ADVANCE-MM)
column5: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column6:
Metal casting and injection molding is a widely used manufacturing process for producing complex metal parts with high precision. MIM offers a valuable technique for manufacturing complex metal parts. However, a significant challenge lies in achieving uniform cooling throughout the mold. Uneven cooling can lead to warping, distortion, residual stresses, and internal voids, compromising the dimensional accuracy and mechanical properties of the final part. In addition, traditional MIM processes often face challenges related to cycle time optimization. Thus, this project aims to investigate the potential of additive manufacturing (AM) for improving cooling efficiency in metal casting and injection molding. By leveraging the design freedom and capabilities of AM, the project seeks to develop innovative mold designs with optimized cooling channels, ultimately leading to the production of higher-quality metal parts through MIM. This project will also use advanced simulation and analysis to identify the most efficient design for uniform cooling. This will help refine injection pressure, holding pressure, and cooling time parameters to achieve optimal heat transfer and minimize cycle time.

Improved Cooling Efficiency
In metal casting and injection molding, uniform cooling throughout the part is crucial for maintaining dimensional accuracy and minimizing defects. Currently, metal casting and injection molding processes often face challenges with cooling uniformity, leading to part defects and longer cycle times. Uneven cooling rates across the part can cause sections to solidify and shrink at different times. This internal stress can lead to warping and distortion of the final product. Thicker sections, for example, will cool slower and may shrink more compared to thinner sections, causing the part to bend. In addition, non- uniform cooling creates localized thermal gradients within the part. As different areas cool and contract at different rates, residual stresses get locked into the material. These stresses can weaken the part and make it more susceptible to cracking or failure under load. Meanwhile, rapid cooling in some areas can trap gas bubbles within the molten metal, leading to internal voids and porosity. Conversely, slow cooling in thicker sections can promote the formation of larger, less desirable gas pockets. The combined effect of warpage, distortion, and shrinkage due to non-uniform cooling makes it challenging to achieve tight dimensional tolerances. Parts may deviate from the intended size and shape, impacting functionality and requiring additional finishing processes (Park et al., 2020).

Complex Geometry Production
Many industries require intricate metal parts with complex geometries that are difficult to produce using traditional manufacturing methods. MIM struggles with very thin walls due to the flow characteristics of the feedstock. The binder acts as a lubricant during injection, but with thin walls, there might not be enough material to fill the cavity completely, leading to incomplete parts or structural weaknesses. In addition, sharp corners can create flow issues as the feedstock encounters resistance when changing x direction abruptly. This can result in incomplete filling or even cracking at the corners. Regarding internal features, complex internal features, and undercuts can trap binders within the part. The de-binding process might not be able to effectively remove all the binder from these areas, potentially leading to residual stresses, voids, or even part cracking during sintering. Intricate geometries can make achieving a smooth surface finish challenging. The de-binding process might leave behind surface imperfections or require additional finishing steps after sintering, increasing production time and cost (Quarto et al., 2022) (Suwanpreecha & Manonukul, 2022).

Cycle Time Optimization
Minimizing production cycle times is crucial for enhancing productivity and reducing manufacturing costs in high-volume production environments. Traditional mold manufacturing techniques can restrict the design of cooling channels, leading to uneven cooling throughout the part. This necessitates longer cooling times to ensure proper solidification and prevent defects like warping or cracking (Virdhian et al., 2012).

Solution
Metal Additive Manufacturing (AM): Utilize metal AM technologies to fabricate MIM tooling with integrated conformal cooling channels, allowing for precise control over cooling rates and uniformity. AM allows for the rapid creation of prototype molds for MIM. This enables designers to iterate on mold designs quickly and efficiently, optimizing cooling channels and part geometry before committing to expensive traditional mold manufacturing processes. In addition, complex mold inserts with intricate features, such as those required for undercuts or internal cavities, can be additively manufactured. These inserts can then be integrated into a conventionally manufactured mold base, offering a cost-effective approach to achieving complex mold functionalities.

Conformal Cooling Design
Innovative mold design techniques like conformal cooling channels can help achieve more uniform cooling, reducing the risk of warping and distortion. Unlike traditional mold manufacturing techniques, where designs of cooling channels are very limited, additive manufacturing allows the creation of intricate, conformal cooling channels that precisely follow the part's contours. This enables more uniform cooling throughout the mold, reducing the risk of warping, distortion, and residual stresses in the final MIM product. Moreover, AM facilitates the creation of complex cooling channel designs for optimization and testing. Different cooling channel configurations can be additively manufactured and tested with the MIM process to determine the most efficient design for uniform cooling of the final part.

Advanced Simulation and Analysis
Employ advanced simulation tools to analyze thermal performance and optimize cooling channel configurations for maximum efficiency.AM also facilitates the creation of samples with slight variations in material composition or processing parameters. By analyzing the behavior of these samples through simulation, valuable insights into the sensitivity of the MIM process to material variations and optimize process parameters for consistent results. AM also enables the creation of digital models of molds with complex cooling channels or intricate features. These models can be integrated with simulation software to test the effectiveness of different cooling strategies and mold designs. This allows for optimization of the mold design for uniform cooling and minimization of potential defects before physical mold construction.

Differentiation
Implementing conformal cooling in MIM tooling sets our project apart by addressing cooling challenges in a novel and efficient manner. This technique of leveraging metal AM technologies enables the production of complex tooling designs that are not achievable with traditional methods, offering a competitive edge. By improving cooling efficiency and reducing cycle times, our approach enhances overall productivity and cost-effectiveness compared to conventional MIM processes.

Benefit
The application of metal additive manufacturing to metal casting and/or injection molding leads to creation of inserts that are optimized for cooling since it can create intricate conformal cooling channels that are complicated to produce using conventional manufacturing. This conformal cooling reduces part warpage and defects, leading to higher-quality finished products. This will hopefully lead to improvement of cooling and cycle times resulting in increased throughput and faster production of metal parts. Moreover, reduced defects, lower cycle times, and improved productivity contribute to overall cost savings in manufacturing operations. The project will promote the adoption of metal AM and conformal cooling technologies in the MIM industry, driving innovation and competitiveness.

column4: Connected and Unified Autonomous Technologies with Automation and Robotics (CUATRO): A Showcase of Industry 4.0 Capabilities in Various Industries
column5: Metals Industry Research and Development Center
column6:
The Philippines, boasting a decade of experience as a legacy manufacturer, now seeks to upgrade the value of its manufactured goods. This ambitious endeavor demands resources and capabilities previously unavailable. In comparison to its ASEAN counterparts—Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Vietnam, the Philippine government's role in implementing Industry 4.0 remains relatively weak. The Philippines lacks a reliable internet infrastructure as do many of its ASEAN neighbors. However, one of the obstacles to successful adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies lies in the Filipino education and research initiatives. Given the critical role of education and research institute in Industry 4.0 development, the country will have a challenging time building the manufacturing skills and production capabilities they need. Low level of research funding, a lack of skills training and little progress in developing technical degree programs are the culprits.  

In 2018, DOST-MIRDC initiated the Establishment of Advanced Mechatronics, Robotics, and Industrial Laboratory (AMERIAL) focuses on advancing industrial automation technologies, such as mechatronics, robotics, and control systems. This facility offers a range of services, including research and development, training, and technical consultancy, primarily aimed at enhancing the skills and capabilities of M&E industries, academic institutions, and other stakeholders in the field of industrial automation. After the project implementation of AMERIAL last 2021, the project team has arrived on the following takeaways from the extensive conduct of technology needs assessment on MSMEs across various industries; (1) majority of MSMEs have not yet arrive in a manufacturing scale that can take advantage of automation. (2) it was established at the time that the country’s readiness for taking advantage of Industry 4.0 is still inadequate and (3) it was identified that there is a lack of technical knowledge about available new technologies, financial aspects, lack of technically skilled workers, and other socio-cultural and organizational issues are influencing the low technology adoption of MSMEs. 

The Philippines has seen significant economic growth recently, but it is still considered a legacy economy with a robust production foundation yet lacking readiness for Industry 4.0 manufacturing, as stated in the ASEAN National Industry 4.0 Initiatives article. ASEAN six countries generally share the same problems of modernizing their education systems, training workers with useful skills and improving infrastructures so vital to Industry 4.0 readiness. The main difference, however is the role that different national government plays in the industry 4.0 adoption process, like Singapore, the Philippine government should initiate and be a champion in modernizing its manufacture base. The government agencies should offer monetary incentives, infrastructure, and software tools. They also support many opportunities for manufacturers and other stakeholders to build relationships that are essential to digital transformation.   

In line with this vision, the DOST- MIRDC proposing a program on Establishment of a Smart Factory demonstrating Industry 4.0 architecture focusing on core technologies including Autonomous Robots, Simulation, System Integration, Internet of Things (IoT), Additive Manufacturing, and Augmented and Virtual Reality (AR/VR). Industry 4.0, characterized by the fusion of digital technologies and physical systems, promises significant advancements in productivity, efficiency, and innovation across industries. The era of Industry 4.0 presents an unparalleled opportunity to transform industries, drive innovation, and elevate economic growth through the integration of advanced technologies such as Smart Manufacturing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), 5G, and others. 

This program outlines a strategic framework aimed at fostering capability building, research and development, and industry-university collaboration to propel nations towards a future characterized by a higher share of Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) intensive sectors in GDP by:
1. establishing a robust ecosystem for Industry 4.0 that promotes innovation, fosters collaboration between academia and industry, and accelerates the adoption of advanced technologies.
2. driving research and development initiatives focused on Autonomous Robots, Internet of Things (IoT), Additive Manufacturing (AM), System Integration, Augmented Reality, and Simulation, thereby enhancing industrial capabilities and competitiveness.
3. facilitating the transition of industries towards STI intensive sectors, thereby enhancing productivity, efficiency, and sustainability.

column4: Continuation of 8-Storey Student Center, Innovation Hub and Educational Complex, (USTP CDO), (Phase 2 and Phase 3)
column5: University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines
column6:
The 8-Storey Student Center and Educational Complex at the University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines (USTP) aims to enhance the campus’s educational and support infrastructure while addressing critical environmental and safety challenges. This second phase of development focuses on elevating key areas to higher floors, creating expansive open spaces at the ground level. This design not only maximizes functionality but also mitigates risks associated with the campus's location in a flood-prone area.

The strategic elevation of essential offices and learning spaces reflects a commitment to disaster resilience, especially given the campus's position on marshland near the Bitan-ag Creek. With parts of the USTP Cagayan de Oro Campus already vulnerable to flooding, further development must consider the impact of impermeable surfaces on water absorption. Preserving green spaces and marshlands is vital to maintain the campus’s ecological balance and reduce the risks posed by flooding.

This initiative aligns with USTP's mission to provide a safe, inclusive, and innovative learning environment for its community. The integration of sustainability principles ensures that the complex not only meets the immediate needs of students, faculty, and staff but also serves as a model for resilient infrastructure.

The project supports the USTP Framework 2030, which emphasizes sustainable and innovative infrastructure aligned with national priorities such as the Philippine Development Plan and Regional Development Investment Program (RDIP). It contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), specifically: Quality Education (SDG 4), Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11), Climate Action (SDG 13), and Sustainability and Climate Resilience. 

The design prioritizes climate change resilience through elevated construction and the preservation of natural water absorption areas. These measures reflect USTP’s commitment to sustainable practices and infrastructure that can withstand environmental challenges. In response to this, Project DESAL (Desalination for Enhanced Sustainable Aquatic Living) seeks to harness advanced desalination technologies to convert seawater into sustainable freshwater.

This project is designed to align with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028, which highlights the need for sustainable water management, environmental preservation, and the enhancement of public health and economic resilience. Project DESAL focuses on the development of innovative and scalable desalination systems that will not only increase freshwater availability but also ensure the process remains environmentally sustainable and economically feasible.

Project DESAL aims to address the increasing demand for freshwater, particularly in regions with unreliable or insufficient sources. By leveraging cutting-edge desalination technologies, the project will create a more resilient water infrastructure, supporting both urban and rural communities. Additionally, it will emphasize eco-friendly approaches to desalination, prioritizing sustainability in the production and distribution of freshwater.

column4: ESTABLISHMENT OF ABACA BIOTECHNOLOGY LABORATORIES (IN SUPPORT OF THE ABACA TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION CENTER OF CATANDUANES STATE UNIVERSITY) AT MAIN CAMPUS
column6:
Catanduanes remains the country’s leading abaca-producing province. In 2024, it produced 20,371.43 metric tons of abaca fiber, representing about 31.5% of national output and 91% of the abaca production in the Bicol Region. Supporting this is its substantial abaca-planted area, about 24,734.69 hectares, or roughly 19% of the national total. Despite damage from typhoons, Catanduanes continues to lead in abaca production. While earlier averages from 2010–2019 showed higher annual production (about 22,500 MT), recent data suggests there has been a moderate decline from those levels. (Philippine Statistics Authority - RSSO V. (2025, May 24); PhilFIDA, 2021)

Given the economic and agricultural importance of the abaca industry to the province and the country, the establishment of specialized biotechnology laboratories is crucial to sustaining and enhancing production capacity. The proposed facility will integrate advanced research and development capabilities for the collection and maintenance of high-quality abaca planting materials, protein-based and nucleic acid-based virus detection, and micro- and macro-propagation techniques for producing disease-free planting stocks. These laboratories will also support enhancements across the abaca value chain, ensuring quality control and the preservation of genetic diversity through germplasm conservation and the maintenance of a field genebank.

The Abaca Biotechnology Laboratories will be equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure to enable precise diagnostics and standardized propagation protocols. Virus detection methods will follow established references, such as the Manual on Protein-Based and Nucleic Acid-Based Detection Techniques for Abaca Viruses (PhilFIDA Research Division in collaboration with UP Diliman-NIMBB, 2017) and the Harmonized Tissue Culture Protocols for PhilFIDA Laboratories (2018). Additionally, the project will contribute to establishing the geographical indication (GI) of abaca for the Bicol Region, which will strengthen the industry’s branding, traceability, and market competitiveness.

This initiative directly supports the Philippine Development Plan’s sector outcomes on expanding opportunities in agriculture, forestry, and fisheries and advancing science, technology, and innovation for sustainable development. By improving disease management, ensuring the supply of genetically robust planting materials, and fostering technology-driven value chain improvements, the project will enhance productivity, safeguard livelihoods, and reinforce the position of Catanduanes as the national leader in abaca production.

column4: REMOVE As – Radiation Technology for Efficient Mitigation Of Contaminated Valuable Waters Containing Arsenic
column6: In areas where the drinking water contains unsafe levels of arsenic, the immediate concern is finding a safe source of drinking water, and if this cannot be established, the short-term goal is to reduce arsenic levels. The Dutch Risk Reduction-Team Mission that surveyed and studied the high-arsenic level areas in the Philippines suggested that “it is very likely that treatment based on adsorption or enhanced coagulation, possibly supported by an appropriate pre-treatment will result in more reliable, effective and efficient arsenic removal”. In this project, a modified nonwoven fabric will be synthesized and applied as an arsenic adsorbent. The iron oxide-coated polypropylene-based adsorbent for arsenic removal will be produced through the radiation-grafting technology. Given the potential merits of the iron oxide-coated fibrous adsorbent produced through radiation-grafting, it is expected to perform better than both the commercial adsorbent and the DRR-Team recommended IHE ADART process. In areas with high arsenic levels, the proposed technology may be easily installed in household water faucets. It may also be installed in the treatment plants of water districts to provide clean and safe water to its customers. The project team aims to work with a Balibago Water Works and La Trinidad water concessionaires in the development and testing of the adsorbent.

column4: STRENGTHENING BUKIDNON STATE UNIVERSITY’S RESEARCH CAPACITY: A Strategic Proposal to Increase Research Funding for Regional and National R&D Growth
column6:
Northern Mindanao’s R&D intensity stands at only 0.09% of GRDP, achieving just 12.2% of the RDP 2028 target of 0.74%. This reflects a massive 87.8% gap in
research investment. Meeting the target would require an eightfold increase in R&D expenditure (DOST Region X, 2024). The region’s R&D personnel density is 226 full-time equivalent (FTE) researchers per million population— far below the RDP-X 2028 target of 305, leaving a 25.9% personnel gap. Addressing this will require adding at least 79 FTEs per million population (DOST Region X, 2024).

These persistent deficits signal the urgent need for increased and sustained public investment in R&D, particularly through higher education institutions. As a state university, BukSU plays a pivotal role in driving local innovation ecosystems. Its underfunding not only hampers institutional development but also weakens Northern Mindanao’s ability to meet its R&D and inclusive growth goals. Strategic budget support to BukSU will directly strengthen the region’s capacity to produce knowledge-based, policy-relevant solutions for national development.

From 2015 to 2024, BukSU’s GAA research allocation remained critically low—averaging only around ₱1.2 million annually—with only two temporary spikes in 2018 and 2020. This funding level has not kept pace with BukSU’s expanding research mandates and academic population. Over the past five years, BukSU’s average research budget per faculty member has hovered at
approximately ₱2,500 annually—a figure drastically below what is required to support independent, competitive, or collaborative research. This severely
constrains faculty productivity and institutional innovation.

To address these persistent gaps, BukSU respectfully requests the DBM’s support in increasing its annual GAA
research allocation to ₱19,642,024.12 beginning FY 2026. This strategic budget adjustment will support:
Research Publication Incentives for Scopus-indexed outputs;
Conference Presentation and Recognition Support at local and international levels;
Seed Grants for Faculty-Initiated Research aligned with regional priorities;
Publication Fee Assistance and Best Paper Incentives

column4: FROM STREAM TO TABLE: Fostering Biodiversity, Ensuring Food and Water Security through Collaborative Watershed Management
column6:
The town of Quinapondan, named after the Samareño word “Kinapul-an,” once thrived on abundant food from fertile lands and bountiful seas. However, modern human activities—like agricultural encroachment, illegal poaching, and mangrove destruction—have severely diminished food and water resources. This has led to a 40% reduction in potable water due to watershed degradation, harming local biodiversity and agricultural productivity.
 
In the 1980s, an irrigation system expanded irrigated rice farming to 285 hectares, producing 1,140 metric tons per cropping (PhP52,440,000). Unfortunately, neglect has reduced this area to just 61 hectares, resulting in a loss of 896 tons per cropping (PhP11,224,000) and a 78.6% decrease in farmers’ incomes. This project seeks to rehabilitate the irrigation infrastructure, increase water supply, and enhance rice productivity while establishing a Level III Water System for 2,576 households; boosting local government revenues.
 
Implementing circular economic practices in water management and producing organic fertilizer from municipal waste will support sustainable agriculture (ube & rice). This may be achieved by allocating 5% of the income from drinking water consumption and 3% share from irrigated rice production as payments to ecosystem services (PES). Additionally, the adoption of Rainforestation-Aquilaria farming will promote community livelihoods and contribute to local economic growth.

column4: Fisheries Information and Small-boat Integrated Smart-tracking and Human-safety Network (FISHNET) Project
column6:
With the aim of controlling illegal, unreported, unregulated (IUU) fishing and overfishing, the government thru the Republic Act 10654: Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing, mandates the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources to implement Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) to track fishing activities around the country [1]. As larger commercial vessels are already equipped with an AIS system for vessel monitoring, small fishing vessels which make up a majority in the country are currently untracked. 

A survey conducted from May 2015 to October 2016 in the coastal barangays of Cavite, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, and Metro Manila recorded a total of 3,659 fishing boats from 84 coastal barangays or about 40% out of the 212 coastal barangays in Manila Bay. About 94.45% of the boats are municipal fishing boats, and only 5.55% are commercial boats. [2] 

The proposed research project aims to address this gap by developing an end-to-end system that will enable authorities to track, analyze and monitor the small fishing boats in various fishing areas across the Philippines. This would include the development of: 
• small independent hardware devices to be installed in fishing boats 
• base station to receive and collect all the data and retransmit to central server 
• visualization software for analysis and monitoring 

In addition, the system will serve as a tool for tracking fishing boats during emergencies. Authorities can use it to determine a vessel’s last known location, thereby expediting search and rescue operations.

column4: AquaSentinel: An AI-Enabled Autonomous Buoy and Uncrewed Boat System for Continuous Water Quality and Environmental Monitoring
column6: Description: This proposal outlines a hybrid and scalable multi-robot coordinated system for real-time water quality and weather monitoring using three stationary buoys, three autonomous USVs, a GCS (Ground Control Station) for supervisory coordination and docking hub, and augmented by a Jarvis-like AI agent for intelligent decision-making and user interaction. For the hardware details, prototypes originating from Metbuoy+ and STRIIIDER project will be reproduced and customized to add interfaces for agent control. The system operates on a "sleep-wake" protocol: The 3 Sentry buoys continuously monitor separate zones of a water body. Upon detecting an anomaly (e.g., pH drop or turbidity spike), the specific buoy alerts the GCS. The GCS then acts as "Mission Control," selecting an available docked boat or fleet for swarm formation, uploading the specific target coordinates, and deploying it to investigate and map the pollution source using AI vision.

column4: Mapping, Scoping, and Profiling BARMM Textiles towards Developing Textile Inclusive Innovation Ecosystem
column6:
The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is a self-governing political and territorial entity guided by its Organic Law. Its socio-economic activities and customary laws substantially function as reiterations of its Moro roots and representation. Similarly, the abundance and persistence of artistic material culture, such as textiles and other textile-related arts (hand woven mats, beadwork, and embroidery needlecrafts) attest to its ethno-religious identity.

Furthermore, by promoting stingless beekeeping, this will strengthen sustainable agriculture and rural livelihoods through continued research, training, and policy advocacy. However, despite of their ecological and economic potential, stingless bee populations remain understudied compared to their honeybee counterparts. Hence, this project includes a systematic study on their biology, foraging behavior, physiochemical properties and nutritional composition of honey, pot-pollen, and propolis, and potential livelihood from stingless beekeeping, and gearing towards meliponitourism.

column4: Feasibility Study on the Establishment of Iligan Cancer Research (iCARE) Diagnosis and Treatment Center in MSU-IIT
column5: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology
column6:
Cancer is among the leading causes of death in the Philippines. Outside major urban centers, patients face high out-of-pocket costs, limited treatment capacity, and uneven geographic distribution of services—conditions that delay care, interrupt treatment, and worsen outcomes, especially for families with limited means.

Iligan and nearby municipalities are not exempt. Many patients travel to Cagayan de Oro City or farther for consultations, imaging, and radiotherapy. Transport and lodging expenses, time away from work, and long travel times create financial toxicity and contribute to treatment interruptions and loss to follow-up.

To address these gaps, MSU-IIT proposes the Iligan Cancer Research (iCARE) Center—a radiotherapy-enabled, research-active hub that would bring core services closer to patients, improve continuity of care, and reduce non-medical costs. The center is also envisioned to catalyze regional development by creating high-skill jobs (radiation oncologists, medical physicists, radiation therapists, oncology nurses, biomedical engineers, IT/administrative staff), attracting vendor activity, and strengthening the local health ecosystem through evidence-based practice and research.

iCARE further supports national workforce development. With most Medical Physics graduate programs concentrated in Metro Manila, iCARE would provide a compliant clinical training site and research infrastructure for thesis work, faculty scholarship, student rotations/residencies, and industry-partnered innovation—building a sustainable pipeline of expertise for Visayas–Mindanao and the country.

Before any construction or equipment decisions, MSU-IIT will undertake a feasibility study to determine whether an Iligan-based cancer center is warranted, what configuration best fits community needs, and how it can be made clinically sound, compliant, and sustainable. The study will:

(1) Quantify demand in Iligan and neighboring LGUs using PhilHealth claims, hospital referrals, tumor registries, and patient travel/queue data.

(2) Produce a regulatory roadmap (DOH approved radiation facilities and devices, radiation safety, environmental and biomedical waste, building/fire/zoning, and data privacy) to define design-shaping requirements.

(3) Develop a conceptual building brief with functional adjacencies, shielding and utility provisions, IT needs, and an expansion-ready layout.

(4) Benchmark clinical workflows and staffing models through structured visits to established cancer centers and explore training/research collaborations.

These outputs will enable an evidence-based decision and, if warranted, guide subsequent schematic design and approvals.
MSU-IIT will undertake a 1 year feasibility study to determine the viability, optimal configuration, and requirements for establishing the Iligan Cancer Research (iCARE) Center in Iligan City. The study will quantify service demand across Iligan and nearby LGUs (PhilHealth claims, hospital referrals, travel/queue data), produce a DOH/FDA-aligned regulatory and licensing roadmap (radiation safety, environmental/biomedical waste, building/fire/zoning, data privacy), and develop a conceptual building & service brief covering functional adjacencies, shielding and utility provisions, ICT integration, and future expansion. It will also benchmark workflows, QA, throughput, and staffing via structured visits to established cancer centers and pursue collaboration MOUs for training and research. Outputs—demand projections, regulator-aligned requirements, a concept brief, and phased options with key risks—will support an evidence-based decision for subsequent schematic design.

column4: Development of a Small-Scaled Dredging Unit for Flood Mitigation in Urban Areas

Cebu City currently spends around ₱13.6M annually on manual canal and drainage cleaning, while conventional dredging systems typically cost ₱50M–₱100M. The proposed portable system is estimated at ₱15.6M, with projected ROI of 30% and IRR of 26% over a 10-year useful life.

The project will be developed with Innomech Tooling and Engineering Services for machine design and fabrication, and three private firms—Mindanao Global Resources Corporation, CBG Group of Companies, and Archi Global Company—have expressed strong intent to adopt the technology and offer land-based dredging services to LGUs.

column4: Design and Development of Leak Testing Equipment for Steel Drum Manufacturing using Energy dissipation and Pressure Decay Method
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6:
Steel drum manufacturing—especially for containers used for hazardous or sensitive materials—requires strict quality control, and leak testing is a key requirement. This project will improve the steel drum production process at Mindanao Container Corporation (MCC) by addressing defects identified through a root-cause analysis by USTP Jasaan faculty, which found that rejects were largely driven by surface rust caused by water used in the current leak-detection setup. In addition, the existing method cannot detect micro-leaks below 0.2 mm, which is required by a customer for tight-head triple-seamed drums.

To resolve these issues, the researchers propose an automated leak-testing system using the pressure decay method. While pressure decay typically requires longer holding times than alternatives (e.g., tracer gas or negative pressure), the project will reduce this limitation by determining the optimal pressure variation through analysis of energy dissipation of pressurized air inside the drum. The work will involve designing, fabricating, and testing specialized equipment, with the expectation of improving detection reliability, shortening test time, reducing downtime, and ultimately strengthening MCC’s product quality, financial performance, and industry reputation.

column4: Pre-commercialization of MUCAS-4H Technology for Enhanced Lettuce Production
column5: Philippine Council for Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development

This proposal presents the pre-commercialization plan for MUCAS-4H, an innovative, locally developed smart hydroponics system tailored to enhance lettuce production in the Philippines. Developed with support from the DOST-CRADLE program, MUCAS-4H integrates Internet of Things (IoT) technology with automated control mechanisms to monitor and regulate key environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, pH, and nutrient levels. The system is complemented by a user-friendly mobile application that allows farmers to manage operations remotely, ensuring real-time data access and responsive decision-making. By automating critical tasks and enabling precise control of growing conditions, MUCAS-4H significantly increases crop yield, reduces labor dependency, and promotes continuous, climate-resilient farming. Its modular, scalable design makes it ideal for both smallholder and commercial farms, providing a sustainable, technology-driven solution to modern agricultural challenges.

During pilot deployment at Ephrathah Farms, MUCAS-4H demonstrated a 67% improvement in yield, translating to an estimated Php 25,000 in additional monthly income for a 120-square-meter greenhouse with 1,800 butterhead lettuce plants. The system's performance validates its potential to significantly boost farm productivity and profitability.

The proposed project seeks to upgrade the current prototype into a commercial-grade, field-deployable unit. It involves refining the system design, validating performance across diverse farm conditions, conducting market and intellectual property studies, and building a sustainable commercialization plan in support of Republic Act 10055, also known as the “Philippine Technology Transfer Act of 2009.”

column4: Composite Textiles for Home, Furniture and other Creative Applications
column5: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development
column6: The local furniture industry is facing challenges regarding the availability of local sustainable materials for furniture. With the abundance of natural textile fibers (NTF) in the Philippines, this challenge can be addressed. The DOST-PTRI has developed the technologies that transform these textile fibers into various textile assemblies such as yarns, weaves, knits, and nonwovens, each possessing unique properties for different applications. These materials will be consolidated into a textile material library that indicates material properties and basic information to provide the local creative industries a centralized material resource. A selection of these will be engineered into a composite textile that will be suitable for upholstery applications. A handloom woven textile will serve as the top layer of the composite, followed by a nonwoven textile in the middle, and lastly a powerloom woven textile at the bottom.  These individual textile components will be combined through lamination technologies, developing a novel composite textile material that possesses the combined properties of each of the individual textile components. Parameters of the lamination process will be varied to produce the composite with the most preferable set of properties in the context of furniture applications. Through this Project, local upholstery will be more sustainable, visually appealing, and its technical characteristics will comply with international standards for upholstery, addressing the needs of the local furniture industry for localized capability and sustainable materials.

column4: ASEAN Space Data Infrastructure Project
column6:
The ASEAN Space Data Infrastructure (ASEAN-SDI) is a regional initiative proposed by the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) to strengthen Earth Observation (EO) and communications capabilities across ASEAN Member States. EO has emerged as an indispensable decision-making tool for governments and industries alike, underpinning effective action in disaster management, agriculture, maritime domain awareness, climate monitoring, and digital inclusion. ASEAN Member States have recognized their strategic value, as evidenced in the Deloitte Southeast Asia Space Industry Report, which reflects the variety of EO satellites being deployed to meet national needs. As the region’s space sector becomes more mature and dispersed, such deployments are expected to increase, representing a budding opportunity for ASEAN to consolidate efforts and harness shared value from these investments. In parallel, the region’s rapid digital transformation and the persistent connectivity gap across many communities highlight the need for stronger satellite communications infrastructure. By integrating a data relay system (DRS) and telecommunications payload into the ASEAN-SDI, the project seeks not only to accelerate EO data delivery but also to expand broadband access and provide a resilient digital backbone for the region.

The ASEAN-SDI responds directly to this trajectory. It will establish a regional space data highway that integrates two complementary segments: a constellation of Earth Observation satellites and a geostationary relay satellite with dual functions for data relay and telecommunications. Together, these segments will provide near real-time, high-capacity space data services tailored to ASEAN’s needs. The EO component ensures the region can generate timely and reliable data, while the GEO relay segment overcomes current bottlenecks in downlink and connectivity by enabling optical inter-satellite links and high-throughput communications. This combination enhances the speed and reliability of EO data delivery while simultaneously offering bandwidth services to support connectivity and resilience.

This proposal is also cognizant of the spurring EO satellite deployments already underway across ASEAN. Member States possess distinct strengths in technology, research, and logistics, but they face similar challenges in ensuring access to data and connectivity. These common needs are reflected in the satellites they have launched, as reported by Deloitte, and demonstrate both the demand and the opportunity for a shared ASEAN-wide infrastructure. By providing an integrated EO and relay system, ASEAN-SDI will not only meet these needs but also position the region to take advantage of economies of scale and interoperability.

Beyond improving the speed of data transmission, ASEAN-SDI aims to enhance regional self-reliance, reduce dependence on external providers, and strengthen digital and space infrastructure integration. Structured as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) with blended financing, it offers a bankable and scalable model that balances public sector objectives with private sector efficiency. column4: Project for Capacity Enhancement on Traffic Management with Improvement of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) in Metropolitan Manila
column6:
In Metropolitan Manila, economic and population growth, along with rapid motorization, have led to severe traffic congestion, resulting an estimated  economic loss of approximately USD96 million per day (JICA survey, 2019). This congestion contributes to various challenges, including air pollution and poor mobility of people and goods. To address these issues, infrastructure development is essential. Several major projects such as the construction of railways and highways are currently underway, however, completion will take a longer time. While the construction of this infrastructure is in progress, traffic demand continues to rise. Consequently, it is necessary to implement short-term congestion mitigation measures and strengthen the human resource and institutional capacities necessary for effective  traffic management.

As an immediate response to congestion, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), with support from JICA, implemented the "Project for the Formulation of a Comprehensive Traffic Management Plan for Metropolitan Manila" from 2019 to 2022 (hereinafter referred to as the "CTMP"). Through the CTMP, MMDA as the counterpart agency and the Japan Expert Team (JET) identified strategic directions for traffic management and formulated a five-year Traffic Management Action Plan. Within this plan, “ITS Development for Traffic Management" and "Development of a Database System" were identified as priority initiatives.

Strengthening technical and planning capabilities plays a significant role in ensuring the effective implementation of these initiatives. Thus, the "Project for Capacity Enhancement on Traffic Management with Improvement of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) in Metropolitan Manila", was proposed to support the said objectives.

column4: ISSDA4PH: INNOVATIVE SMART SYSTEMS FOR DATA-DRIVEN AQUACULTURE TO PROMOTE A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE PHILIPPINES: Project 1. SPATSS: Smart Production and Advanced Technologies for Sustainable Seedstock Supply in Hatcheries
column6:
The aquaculture industry in the Philippines provides critical income for small-scale fishers and affordable protein for the population. Yet, it remains constrained by traditional practices and long-standing challenges such as pollution, harmful algal blooms, poor fry and seed supply, and inadequate infrastructure.

The National Fisheries Development Center (NFDC) and University of the Philippines - Visayas (UPV) operate aquaculture hatcheries that produce green mussel seeds, but this falls short of meeting local demand due to environmental constraints, particularly poor water quality, and inconsistent natural food production. To address these issues, this project will develop a compact Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) to regulate water quality in larval rearing and nursery tanks, enabling year-round fry or seed production. A photobioreactor will also ensure a consistent algae supply for larvae, improving feeding efficiency.

The project aims to increase hatchery productivity, improve larval survival, and promote sustainable aquaculture farming by integrating smart technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and automation.

column4: ISSDA4PH: INNOVATIVE SMART SYSTEMS FOR DATA-DRIVEN AQUACULTURE TO PROMOTE A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE PHILIPPINES: Project 2. SAGANA: Smart Aquaculture Feeder for Enhancing Feed Distribution in Grow-out Operations
column6:
This research project aims to develop a demand-based shrimp feeding system that utilizes IoT technologies, sensory data and feeding curves. The system aims to automatically dispense accurate amounts of shrimp feed 24/7 based on feeding behaviors and environmental data.

The project's primary objective is to address feed wastage caused by human error and untimely feed dispensing. This initiative also brings significant benefits to the metals and engineering sector, specifically to system integrators, by fostering innovation and expanding the application of machine learning and sensory technologies in aquaculture operations, thereby creating opportunities for local entrepreneurs and startup companies. These can stimulate economic growth within the IOT-based industry, enhancing expertise and capacity in machine learning and system integration.

Further, by addressing the technical challenges associated with developing demand-based feeding systems, this research project contributes to the broader goals of sustainable and efficient animal feed production. The prototype will be designed and developed by MIRDC, while testing activities will be supported by the project partner – Marvel Shrimp Farm in Oriental Mindoro.

column4: ISSDA4PH: INNOVATIVE SMART SYSTEMS FOR DATA-DRIVEN AQUACULTURE TO PROMOTE A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE PHILIPPINES: Project 3. New Approaches in Nano-Bubble Oxygenation for Advanced and Innovative Resource Systems in Aquaculture (NANO AIRS) Using Renewable Energy
column6: This research explores innovative methods for improving oxygenation in sustainable aquaculture through the use of nano-bubble technology, integrated with renewable energy. The study is focused on optimizing the oxygenation process in an in-pond raceway system (IPRS), where nano-bubbles enhance water circulation and dissolve oxygen efficiently. Nano-bubbles, due to their small size, offer prolonged oxygen retention in the water, benefiting aquatic life while maintaining water quality. Powered by renewable energy sources such as solar, the system aims to eliminate the reliance on traditional energy-intensive aeration systems, reducing the carbon footprint of aquaculture operations. This combination of technology and sustainability aligns with the growing demand for eco-friendly aquaculture practices. The research will test the effectiveness of nano-bubbles in improving fish productivity, water quality, and overall system efficiency within the IPRS framework. Ultimately, this study aims to advance sustainable aquaculture by reducing energy consumption, enhancing oxygen distribution, and promoting environmental conservation.

column4: National Capability Building Program on Artificial Intelligence
column6:
The National Capability-Building Program on Artificial Intelligence is a multi-year initiative that aims to strengthen the Philippine public sector’s capacity to harness AI for more efficient, innovative, and citizen-centered governance. Aligned with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023–2028, the Program supports the country’s economic and social transformation by investing in human capital, accelerating government digitalization, and fostering dynamic innovation ecosystems that enhance service delivery and upskill the public sector workforce. It likewise advances the PDP’s thrust to improve governance and bureaucratic efficiency by enabling agencies to adopt data-driven, technology-enabled approaches in policy formulation, operations, and frontline services.

The Program is organized around a structured design that combines competency standards, progressive learning pathways, and institutional development. A Public Sector AI Competency Framework defines the skills and proficiency levels expected of senior officials, highly technical experts, and the broader government workforce, and serves as the basis for an integrated training architecture. Using this framework, the Program rolls out a three-phase learning pathway—Priming, Deepening, and Designing—for three main groups: high-level decision-makers, technical specialists and trainers, and general personnel. Priming builds foundational AI literacy and awareness; Deepening provides advanced exposure, hands-on practice, and global benchmarking; and Designing guides participants in developing concrete AI use cases, policies, and prototypes for their agencies. These are supported by an AI microcredential scheme, digital learning platforms, and preparatory work for a National AI Institute that will serve as a hub for sustained capability-building, knowledge sharing, and multi-sector collaboration in support of the PDP’s long-term transformation agenda.

column4: ISSDA4PH: INNOVATIVE SMART SYSTEMS FOR DATA-DRIVEN AQUACULTURE TO PROMOTE A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE PHILIPPINES: Project 5. SortXpert: Precision Sorting Technology for Multi-Commodity Aquaculture Application
column6: Modern technological advances are gradually being adopted in various aquaculture fields that target specific difficulties encountered to increase productivity. Inland municipal aquaculture farming in the Philippines is shifting from traditional extensive farming to an intensive and more efficient setup by adapting modern technological advances. Although aquaculture farming is improving by leaps and bounds, aquaculture harvest and post-harvest practices have yet to adapt to the increasingly labor-intensive practices. Milkfish farming also expands their production in fish cages away from the shores. Development of post-harvest equipment and good practices will enhance the quality of produce and reduce waste. column4: ISSDA4PH: INNOVATIVE SMART SYSTEMS FOR DATA-DRIVEN AQUACULTURE TO PROMOTE A SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE PHILIPPINES: Project 6. Information Systems for Smart Aquaculture (ISSA): Towards Mitigation of Socio-economic Effects of Smart Technologies, Expansion of Yields, Promotion of Environmental Resilience, and Enhancement of Market Access
column6:
This proposed project endeavors to foster smart aquaculture through information and communication technologies and online promotion of products and services that can assist in decision-making for aquaculture species, particularly Asian green mussels and mangrove crabs, by addressing the following industry challenges: a) limited sites for production, b) high mortality rates of juveniles, c) pollution in coastal waters, d) vulnerabilities to climate change, and e) market access. The same tools also promote sustainability, livelihood protection, and traceability of aquaculture products.

The proposed tools to be developed and enhanced are the following: 1) an interactive map that contains water, ecosystem types and environmental parameters in each selected site (i.e., temperature, salinity, chlorophyll, pH, dissolved oxygen, total suspended solids, depth) information that are essential information to be considered in nursery, hatchery, and culture operations of Asian green mussels and mangrove crab species, 2) an interactive model that can provide valuable information on mussel and mangrove crab production vis-à-vis climatic fluctuations, and 3) a web-based application with production and market information for Asian green mussels and mangrove crabs.

These decision-support web-based tools can help guide local government units, national government agencies, non-government units, and interested private parties in identifying potential expansion sites for hatchery and culture of aquaculture commodities, provide forecasts for fluctuating climatic conditions and in mitigating impacts on livelihoods of coastal communities, and supply-driven and demand-driven information to promote market access of mussels and mangrove crabs.

column6: Nile tilapia is an important commodity produced in the Philippines and reared in ponds, cages, and pens. However, its production faces numerous challenges, including maintaining suitable water quality for fish production, maximizing water use, minimizing farm inputs (feeds, fuel), reducing farm operation costs, and the labor-intensive management of raising aquatic species. The project aims to develop several potential aquaculture technologies by infusing precision and digital agriculture technologies, utilization of a renewable energy source in fish production, and the application of engineering principles and sustainable fishery management that could address the issues identified. This project aims to develop and test three prototypes of digitized aqua-technologies namely: smart water management system, smart aqua-feeder, and smart fry collector. The smart water management system aims to provide real-time monitoring of water quality ensuring an automated and appropriate action to maintain the water quality to ideal culture conditions which include, but are not limited to water exchange, provision of aeration, and automatic roll-out of aquashading. The smart aqua-feeder aims to maximize and efficiently feed the fish with reduced human presence. The smart feeder would automatically determine the appetite of the fish during feeding and calculate approximately the biomass of the fish in the culture system. Lastly, the automated fry collector aims to minimize fry mortality, maximize fry collection thus preventing cannibalism among fingerlings, and reduce labor during fry collection in pond-based tilapia hatchery systems. All of these technologies aim to elevate the standard of aquaculture in the Philippines thus making fish farming convenient and attractive to young entrepreneurs.

column4: NATIONAL TILAPIA R&D PROGRAM A. ENSURING ACCESSIBILITY OF FAST STRAIN FOR PRODUCTIVE, PROFITABLE, AND SUSTAINABLE GROW-OUT OPERATIONS: Project 3. Reproductive Performance of FaST Strain Using Propre Boost
column6:
Fish hatchery is an important activity in aquaculture because it is the initial activity in fish aquaculture. One important factor to support the success of tilapia aquaculture is the availability of seeds (Karim et al., 2016). The availability of sustainable seeds and meeting the requirements of good quality and quantity greatly affects the growth of tilapia (Rahman and Awal, 2016).

The yield of broodstock indicates a major obstacle to the production of commercial tilapia. Therefore, expanding our understanding of the variables affecting broodstock production is crucial to the advancement of the culture of tilapia (Coward and Bromage, 2000). The ultimate goal of managing broodstock in hatcheries is to maximize seed yield. Because of the distinctive reproductive characteristics of tilapia, including their early maturation, high frequency of spawning, low fecundity, and high parental care requirements, traditional tilapia seed farming methods have productivity issues. To reliably generate the number of eggs and fry needed by grow-out farms, reproductive development must be programmed with an improved understanding of the proper culture conditions and management techniques for broodfish.

Limited research studies have been done on tilapia specifically on tilapia hatchery using propre boost. Therefore, this study will aim to evaluate the reproductive performance of FaST strain using propre boost.

column4: NATIONAL TILAPIA R&D PROGRAM A. ENSURING ACCESSIBILITY OF FAST STRAIN FOR PRODUCTIVE, PROFITABLE, AND SUSTAINABLE GROW-OUT OPERATIONS: Project 4. Aquaculture Innovations and Strategies for Increased Productivity, Profitability, and Sustainability of Tilapia Grow-Out Production
column6:
The tilapia is one of the most important farmed fish in the Philippines. However, the main issues of concern are the little increase in its production over the years and the low-income during grow-out due to the high cost of production, particularly the feed. One of the major reasons for the low grow-out production is the low survival rate of the fish. To resolve these major issues, this project will increase the grow-out production by innovating the culture system and develop strategies to reduce production cost and/or increase survival of the cultured fish. The project will be comprised of four (4) major components, namely: (1) field testing of the modular culture system to determine the increase in yield per unit production area and survival rate of tilapia; (2) comparative growth trial between tilapia raised in modular culture systems and those raised using traditional methods in private tilapia grow-out farms; (3) assessment of the influence of bioturbator on water quality and total fish yield; and (4) cost and return analysis on the use of modular culture system and bioturbator in tilapia culture.

Preliminary studies at FAC/CLSU on the application of modular culture system (MCS) in tilapia culture showed that MCS increased both the survival and yield. The MCS can enhance tilapia grow-out production by increasing the production cycle/year to 3-5 cycles (at 120 days culture period). Higher survival rates are realized at the MCS up to 94.83%. In addition, MCS can offer better pond management, due to the preparation of the nursery and grow-out phases, for better condition of pond bottom and predator control. MCS can also be a way to improve stock assessment where near the desired stocking density is maintained in every phase of the culture period. Lastly, MCS can economize feeds consumed on the grow-out production by giving the actual amount required and accurate accounting of stock for computation of feeding rates and better FCR. Therefore, increased production cycles/cropping per year and higher survival rate, result to higher grow-out production and higher profits.

column4: eUNIVERSITY ICT AUGMENTATION FOR SUSTAINABLE DIGITAL LEARNING of the Mindanao State University -Maguindanao
column6:
The eUNIVERSITY ICT Augmentation Project of Mindanao State University–Maguindanao aims to modernize the institution’s digital infrastructure, enhance academic and administrative operations, and strengthen sustainable digital learning across all campuses. This initiative is designed to address the increasing demand for technology-enabled education, efficient campus management systems, and secure and reliable connectivity for faculty, staff, and students. Through strategic investments in ICT equipment, software, and network upgrades, the university seeks to transform its traditional learning environment into a fully digital and future-ready institution.

A core component of the project is the procurement of ICT equipment to support office productivity, teaching, and learning. This includes interactive projectors, 4K interactive boards with built-in computers, notebook computers, and inkjet printers for academic units and administrative offices. These tools will empower instructors to deliver dynamic learning experiences while enabling students to engage in more interactive and technology-based activities. Alongside hardware, the project also funds various software subscriptions such as CAD systems, 3D animation tools, AI learning tools, productivity suites, plagiarism detection software, board exam preparation software, virtual meeting platforms, and collaboration systems. These subscriptions ensure that both faculty and students have access to relevant and updated digital tools essential for academic excellence.

To strengthen institutional efficiency, the project includes the development of a comprehensive Campus Management Information System (CMIS). This system integrates academic, administrative, financial, web, library, and document management functions into one unified platform. By digitalizing workflows, the university enhances transparency, minimizes manual processes, and ensures timely access to accurate information.

Another major initiative is the upgrade of traditional classrooms into smart classrooms, which will be equipped with interactive 4K boards, teleconferencing systems, high-performance desktop computers, and UPS units. This modernization enhances hybrid learning implementation and ensures that students can access high-quality instruction regardless of location. Complementary ICT trainings will also be provided to ensure that faculty and staff are fully capable of using these technologies effectively.

The project also establishes a Digital Library to expand access to electronic learning materials. This includes retrofitting existing facilities, installing modern e-library systems, and subscribing to digital library platforms—strengthening research capabilities and supporting remote learning.

A significant infrastructure component is the establishment and upgrade of the campus Data Center, which includes procurement of enterprise-grade servers, installation of data center systems, and comprehensive ICT training. This ensures that the university’s digital services are secure, scalable, and reliable.

To support university-wide connectivity, the project funds the rehabilitation of the campus network infrastructure, installation of structured LAN cabling, and deployment of additional access points. Internet subscription upgrades provide high-speed fiber connections for both Dalican and Annex campuses, ensuring stable and fast access for all users.

Finally, the project includes establishing a Command Center for Surveillance and Security, featuring CCTV cameras, RFID systems, video management platforms, and training for security personnel, ensuring the safety of university assets and stakeholders.

Overall, the eUNIVERSITY ICT Augmentation Project provides a comprehensive blueprint for transforming MSU–Maguindanao into a digitally empowered, secure, and future-ready institution.

column4: NATIONAL TILAPIA R&D PROGRAM A. ENSURING ACCESSIBILITY OF FAST STRAIN FOR PRODUCTIVE, PROFITABLE, AND SUSTAINABLE GROW-OUT OPERATIONS: Project 5. Evaluation of Rearing Performance of FaST and Other Strains in Warm and Cold Conditions
column6:
Tilapia is the most predominant species and second most important cultured fish in the Philippines. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that Tilapia production has contributed about 11% (263,965.3 metric tons) from the total aquaculture of about 2,324,000 metric tons in 2020. However, during the first quarter of 2021, the total volume of fisheries production was registered at 978.62 thousand metric tons. It decreased by 0.8% from the 986.41 thousand metric tons produced during the same period in the previous year (First Quarter Fisheries Situation Report, 2021).

Due to climate change, rise in temperature in ponds is observed. The increase of a few degrees in water temperature can set of ecological changes that will affect most forms of aquatic life (Pandit and Nakamura, 2010). Due to this climate change, several approaches should be undertaken and practice to address the different problems associated with it. For adaptation to climate change, tilapia farming is possible in a wide range of water environments, including freshwater, brackish water, and saltwater conditions. Tilapia can be produced under polyculture, monoculture, and integrated farming in pond systems, cage culture, pen culture, floodplain aquaculture, and coastal ponds. Since tilapia can easily survive in low water volume with high stocking density and short culture duration, this species can be cultured in seasonal water bodies (Rahman et al., 2021).  However, for freshwater fish species, however, the ability to adjust their thermal sensitivity is limited. Therefore, understanding the mechanism underlying the physiological responses in freshwater fishes is key to predicting the effects of climate change on fish population (Portner and Farrel 2008).

This project will evaluate the rearing performance of FaST and other strains (Thailand, Taiwan and Malaysian strain) to be reared in warm-water conditions at different culture environment and culture systems. The result of this project will be an avenue to further develop the tilapia aquaculture industry in the Philippines.

column4: Development of a Green Chemistry Process for Biodegradable Plastics Using Agricultural Residues in Caraga Region
column6: The continued dependence on petroleum-based plastics strains both the environment and the Philippine economy, especially in regions with limited waste management. In Caraga, large volumes of agricultural residues like rice straw, coconut husk, and bagasse are burned or discarded, resulting in pollution and lost value. This project will convert these local residues into bioplastics, reducing reliance on imported materials and supporting a circular economy. The focus is on developing integrated green chemistry pathways for polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) and polylactic acid (PLA). Year 1 will optimize biomass hydrolysis and microbial fermentation at lab scale. Year 2 will scale validated processes to bench-scale and produce bioplastic films for mechanical and biodegradability testing. A techno-economic analysis will gauge competitiveness and guide future scale-up. The project will deliver a documented bench-scale process, SOPs, market-aligned prototypes, and a roadmap for pilot deployment, advancing Caraga’s leadership in sustainable green-materials development and local livelihood growth.

Innovation efforts across the region remain fragmented, with limited linkages among researchers, industry players, investors, and communities. As a result, valuable academic research often fails to reach commercialization, capacity gaps hinder entrepreneurial growth, and economic development remains uneven—favoring urban centers over rural areas.

To address these challenges, the establishment of the Regional Business and Research Center (RBRC) is proposed. The RBRC will serve as an integrated hub for innovation, entrepreneurship, and research translation. It will support research-driven enterprise development, promote business innovation and digital transformation, strengthen MSME competitiveness, and provide policy advisory and economic intelligence. The center will also produce investment project briefs and foster student-industry collaboration, enabling a more connected, inclusive, and innovation-driven regional economy. By bridging gaps in knowledge, resources, and networks, the RBRC will empower Region 12 to unlock its full economic potential and support sustainable, inclusive growth.

column4: PROMOTING HEALTHY FILIPINO LIVER THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY INNOVATIVE RESEARCHES (PHIL LIVER): Project 2. New Diagnostic BiOmarkers for Predicting HBeAg Negative Chronic ViraL HEpatitis in Filipinos (NOBLE)
column6: The New Diagnostic BiOmarkers for Predicting HBeAg Negative Chronic ViraL HEpatitis in Filipinos or NOBLE project aims to determine whether HBcrAg and qHBsAg levels, measured at baseline, can effectively differentiate HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis from HBeAg-negative chronic infection among adult Filipinos. The project will be conducted in six (6) tertiary hospitals in the Philippines wherein participants will be followed prospectively for 12 months, including regular data collection, study assessments, and serial blood sampling at baseline (for the biomarkers) and every three (3) months (for the study assessments). The results of the study will provide the necessary information for a future project, which aims to design and develop a point-of-care test (POCT) using a lateral flow assay using aptamers targeting HBcrAg.

column4: PROMOTING HEALTHY FILIPINO LIVER THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY INNOVATIVE RESEARCHES (PHIL LIVER): Project 3. Microbiome MultI-omiCs to PRedict Outcomes in Chronic Liver Disease (MICRO-CLD)

column4: INTEGRATeD Diagnostics Solutions (IDS): A Portfolio-based R&D Program for the Efficient Development and Preliminary Validation of Protein and Molecular Diagnostic Devices: Project 2. Integrated Diagnostic Solutions for Metabolic Diseases
column6: Through the project, the development of diagnostic tools that target non-communicable diseases such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes will be explored. The main goal of the project is to explore aptamers as an alternative reagent to the diagnosis of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. The use of affinity reagents consisting of aptamers will help provide a potentially more competent and cheaper alternative of screening or companion tests for the Filipino people. Additionally, compared to the traditional reagents, aptamers are easily synthesized, and thus cheaper when creating novel diagnostics. It is through aptamers that the project hopes that it can contribute to the diagnostic field of the Philippines while being an exploratory avenue in learning and manufacturing aptamers for other diseases in the future.

column4: INTEGRATeD Diagnostics Solutions (IDS): A Portfolio-based R&D Program for the Efficient Development and Preliminary Validation of Protein and Molecular Diagnostic Devices: Project 3. Integrated Diagnostic Solutions for Viral Diseases
column6: The AIDS epidemic in the Philippines is one of the fastest growing in Asia and the Pacific Region. Despite this, it is not as prevalent in the country with testing being an important factor in identifying and containing the spread of the virus. The efforts, however, remain hindered by poor accessibility, limited testing sites, and stigma. Hepatitis, on the other hand, is another big public health concern in the country with one in ten people having hepatitis B and six in 1,000 people having hepatitis C. With most infected individuals being asymptomatic for hepatitis, systematic screening for key populations remains inadequate. Similarly, the incidence of dengue globally still seems to be growing dramatically, and despite the fact that the national dengue cases in the Philippines have dropped, there still remains to be 59,675 reported cases in 2020. Central to the transmission reduction efforts of the government is the establishment of community-based testing programs for these viral infections, yet these endeavors appear shortsighted with the continuous increase of cases, like the case for HIV. In alignment with the research priorities of health research and development (R&D), the production of new technologies for diagnostics aiming for early prediction of disease and potential mortality will maximize the possible solutions to these critical health issues. Through the project, the development of timely and essential diagnostic tools that are simpler and cost-effective will offer the intention of promoting rapid screening tests that will then aid in early diagnosis of the viral infections. The use of affinity reagents and methods of amplification for increased sensitivity of detection will provide potentially more competent alternative screening tests in lower resource communities.
