column4: Research-Based Extension Project:  Plastic Bottle Recycling and Reward System (PlasBoReRS)
column6:
This extension project will introduce an innovative solution to plastic bottle waste in Brgy. Salvacion, Lingig, and Brgy. Bucto, Bislig City. The core of the project is the deployment of one automated system that encourages
recycling by providing a tangible incentive. The system itself is designed for user-friendliness and efficiency. Community members can deposit used
plastic bottles into a designated receiving chamber. Integrated sensors, including a light sensor for presence and an
ultrasonic sensor for volume, detect and measure the deposited bottles. A processor then calculates an appropriate
amount of a granular reward (e.g., rice, points, or other pre-determined items) stored in a separate chamber. Upon
processing, the bottle is moved to a collection bin, and the system dispenses the calculated reward to the user. Key features include sensors that monitor the level of the granular reward medium and the fill level of the
bottle collection bin. If the reward supply is low or the collection bin is full, the system temporarily halts acceptance of
new bottles and reward dispensing. An integrated monitor displays status messages, and the system can be
configured to send remote alerts for operator intervention, ensuring continuous and efficient operation. The main
power supply is versatile, compatible with AC/DC sources and potentially solar energy, making it adaptable to local
conditions. One such unit will be strategically placed in [Name of Specific Barangay in Bislig City]. The project will
involve close coordination with the DENR and local barangay officials for site selection, community mobilization, and
ongoing support. IEC campaigns will be conducted to educate residents about the system and the importance of
recycling. Training will be provided to local personnel for basic operation and maintenance. This initiative is expected
to directly contribute to a cleaner coastal environment, increased recycling rates, and enhanced community
engagement in environmental conservation within the barangay.

This study investigates the competencies, work values, and demographic characteristics of barangay treasurers across selected municipalities in Mindanao. As frontline fiscal officers of local communities, barangay treasurers play a critical role in managing public resources, maintaining financial transparency, and ensuring compliance with local government auditing standards. column4: NATURAL ALKALOIDS FOR THE TREATMENT OF METHAMPHETAMINE ADDICTION AND DEPRESSION USING NOVEL ANIMAL MODELS (NATAD): Project 1. The Effects of Berberine and Extinction on Addictive Behavior and Brain Transcriptomics in a Rodent Model of Social-Methamphetamine Addiction
column6:
Methamphetamine (METH) addiction is a worldwide problem accounting for
90% of addiction cases in the Philippines. METH abuse has serious negative
effects on the individual (drug craving, anxiety, poor memory) and society
(crime, loss of productivity). However, there is still no FDA-approved
treatment. High rates of relapse after rehabilitation are often caused by social
factors, particularly in the Philippines, where returning to close-knit
communities re-triggers METH addiction (Asumbrado & Canoy, 2020). Recent
studies in animals have demonstrated that addictive drugs are more rewarding
in the presence of addicted peers (Strickland & Smith, 2014) particularly for
METH (Reyna et al., 2021; Watanabe, 2011). While the social-METH model
would provide the most rigorous test of novel treatments, the project team will
be the first to use this model to evaluate treatments in males and females: 1)
social extinction training to break the social-METH bond, and 2) a naturally
occurring alkaloid berberine, which has shown promise for METH addiction in
two prior studies (from China and Iran). They will use brain transcriptomics
analysis to identify prefrontal-hippocampal genes whose expression correlates
with treatment response, thus constituting novel clinical targets. This project is
relevant to the Philippine context as it provides a potential solution to a
substantial societal problem, affecting both women and men.

column4: NATURAL ALKALOIDS FOR THE TREATMENT OF METHAMPHETAMINE ADDICTION AND DEPRESSION USING NOVEL ANIMAL MODELS (NATAD): Project 2. The Effects of Prophylactic Berberine and Probiotics on the Behavior and Brain Transcriptomics in a Rodent Model of Depressive-Like Behavior
column6:
Depression is a common and serious mental health disorder affecting
individuals of all ages, with women twice as likely to experience depression as
men (Buenaventura et al., 2023; Kessler & Bromet, 2013). It is a global public
health concern, with increasing prevalence over the years. Understanding the
complexity of depression requires analyzing genetic, biochemical, and
behavioral factors. Animal models offer initial evidence on the safety and
efficacy of potential treatments, ensuring that only most promising and safe
treatments advance to human clinical studies. Prior studies have reported that
probiotics initiated prior to stress and extended during and after stress
protected and reversed the effects of depression in male rodents, with few
studies on females. However, their beneficial effect as a prophylactic treatment
(administration limited to pre-stress period) in male and female rodents has
never been investigated. Furthermore, berberine (never given prophylactically)
showed alleviation of mental health disorders but combined treatment with
probiotics was never studied. Using the animal model, the project team can
generate data on potential sex differences and provide preventative
interventions for high-risk individuals (firefighters, emergency medical officers,
police officers).
In this proposal, the researchers aim to investigate the preventive effects of
these treatments on depression-like behaviors and biochemical markers, gut
microbiota, and brain gene expression changes in a rodent model of
depressive-like behavior. They will orally administer probiotics, berberine, or
both treatments for 4 weeks before the induction of depressive-like behavior.

column4: PROGRAM B. PRODUCTIVITY ENHANCEMENT OF SPIN TILAPIA CULTURE SYSTEMS: Project 1. Development of Improved Production System for SPIN Tilapia
column6:
Tilapia, the second most important cultured species in the Philippines, is a key commodity for food security and a source of income for small-scale fish farmers. Despite its potential, the industry has stagnated due to challenges such as low survival rates, disease outbreaks, and climate change. The SPIN tilapia, a hybrid developed to thrive in brackish water and estuarine environments, offers a promising solution to expand production. However, further studies are needed before it can be commercialized.

This project aims to develop innovative production protocols and techniques for SPIN tilapia, focusing on evaluating its reproductive performance in different hatchery systems, determining its growth and survival in high-density grow-out systems, identifying genetic parameters controlling its performance and quality, and developing protocols for its improved hatchery system and high-density grow-out systems. The project leverages best practices in aquaculture, genetics of the SPIN tilapia, and innovative high-density culture systems such as the solar-powered floating in-pond raceway system and the integrated multitrophic aquaculture “IMTA” system with stocked with different species for enhanced economic viability.

The expected outcomes include publications in reputable journals, research outputs dissemination in international conferences, IEC materials, copyrights, and patent applications within 3 years. The project also aims to support research students and staff development through trainings and scholarships, and anticipates acquiring support for future institutional development. This integrated approach aims to improve the production system for SPIN tilapia, thereby advancing the tilapia industry in the Philippines.

The centrifugal spinning device will produce fibers designed for oil adsorption, providing a solution for terrestial and marine oil spill sequestration, while electrospun fibers will be used to modify solar panel glass surfaces to enhance their hydrophobicity, and self-cleaning properties. The long term vision of the project includes designing a scalable centrifugal spinning device and portable electrospinning systems for direct nanofiber deposition on already built surfaces to establish circularity and connection between waste valorization and renewable energy technology.

column4: PROGRAM B. PRODUCTIVITY ENHANCEMENT OF SPIN TILAPIA CULTURE SYSTEMS: Project 2. Development of Feeding Regimen for SPIN Broodstock and Fingerlings
column6: Tilapia are considered one of the most important aquaculture species and represent a major source of protein in many countries, especially in the tropical and subtropical regions. Because of the limited area for freshwater aquaculture and increasing pressure to provide source of cheap and high-quality animal protein into the future, tilapia is now being cultured in brackishwater ponds and in marine cages. This practice led to the development of saline –tolerant tilapia to be able to produce consistently in brackishwater and marine environments. One of the recent strain developed was the Saline-Tolerant O. spirulus x O. niloticus (SPIN) tilapia from the University of the Philippines Visayas. Development of broodstock and fingerlings nutrition and feeding are critical factors for the sustained production of quality eggs and subsequent fry quality that will adopt, grow and survive in a brackish or marine environments. This proposed research will develop the nutrition and feeding regimen for SPIN Tilapia to improve productivity, growth, survival and productivity. This research proposal hopes to increase and sustain production of SPIN Tilapia in the region. The result of this proposal will have a significant contribution to food security and may contribute in the attainment of SDG-2 zero hunger.

column4: PROGRAM B. PRODUCTIVITY ENHANCEMENT OF SPIN TILAPIA CULTURE SYSTEMS: Project 3. Development of Microbial-based High Density Nursery Production for SPIN Tilapia
column6: The stunted growth of the Tilapia industry can be overcome by expanding the culture areas in brackishwater environments. While a suitable O. spirulus x O. niloticus (SPIN) hybrid has been developed to thrive in these environments, the culture of this tilapia - particularly in the nursery phase - has not been optimized. Against this context and considering the financial capacity of the tilapia industry stakeholders, we aim to create a cost-effective culture scheme for the nursery production of SPIN. Thus, for this project, we propose to develop a microbial-based high density nursery production culture system for SPIN. This proposed two (2) year project will include: the comparison of the different microbial based systems with conventional high-density systems for nursery production of tilapia; the optimization of the best performing microbial-based aquaculture system for high density nursery production of saline tilapia and; the economic evaluation of the optimized microbial-based high density nursery culture system. The project is expected to double the volume of available fingerlings for grow-out culture.

column4: Halal Transparent Traceability System with Autonomous IoT Support for Halal and Tayeb Cacao Products (HATTSv2)
column6: Competence of the Philippines' cacao industry is expected to be a key player in the cacao global value chain. However, consumer preferences are focused to know more about the product information from farm to factory. Considering the consumer prospects, HATTS-V1 was proposed and released in June 2023 with the decentralized ledger for saving the farm and factory data and thereby it provided transparency in the chocolate supply chain. However, this version served a limited number of users including the auditing agency only. As an extension with enhanced features for larger audience, we propose a smarter version of a transparent cacao supply chain framework with the combination of loT and blockchain. This extension of HATTS (Halal Transparent Traceability System)-V2, not only provides a digitally transparent ledger for all the stakeholders but also provides features including (1) Integration of lot with blockchain to reduce the human intervention for data entry. The loT ecosystem is proposed to be merged with blockchain by considering sensory data collected via weighing machines, and temperature values involved in manufacturing processes as loT devices. (2) Intelligent reporting feature for support of company's decision-making policy in terms of better understanding of yearly periodic sales w.r.t profit/loss, temperature/weather conditions effect on cacao crops, regional cacao sales, etc. (3) Availability of chocolate manufacturing data to the public (consumer) via QR codes stamped over chocolate product/bar. The proposed system is expected to enhance the supply chain practices with full- fledged support providing data immutability, distribution, and decentralization.

column4: DOST f(x): A Comprehensive Review of the Mandates and the Functions vis-à-vis the Priority Projects of DOST Agencies as a Means of Improving Efficiency in the Delivery of Public Service
column6: During the Senate Plenary Budget Deliberation on the DOST's proposed 2024 budget held on 17 November 2023, the Senate pointed out the seemingly overlapping functions of the DOST and other government offices. As the leading enabler and provider of STI-explicit solutions and in the delivery of public service geared towards a more responsive and efficient bureaucracy, proper delineation of functions among the offices in other national government agencies must be ensured. To achieve this, DOST must review the operations of its different agencies to make a critical analysis of the programs/projects being implemented and necessarily review the DOST's workforce complement in the event that the agencies' functions overlap with one another. Such workforce review is imperative as it is highly likely that agencies performing overlapping functions effectively have redundant human resource complements. Specifically, for purposes of determining whether there is/are duplication/s of functions within and among the agencies, this proposal endeavors to conduct a comprehensive review of their mandates and functions vis-a-vis the priority projects being implemented, conducted, or undertaken by the respective agencies. In the process, the project aims to address and settle any duplication in the exercise of their respective functions in accordance with their governing laws, rules and regulations, and such other pertinent issuances. This effort places greater accountability to the public by the DOST agencies making them more mandate- oriented and expertise-centered government agencies. The endeavor is in line with the efforts to make the bureaucracy more effective, efficient, responsive and progressive. In addressing the abovementioned concern of the Senate, the DOST must ensure that core mandates/functions of the agencies within the institution are aligned with the actual priority projects they implement or conduct and that no single agency performs functions which legally pertain to another.

column4: Z-CharMC: Sequential Self-Supporting Zeolite-Activated Biochar Composite CO2 Capture and Conversion through Fluidized-bed Mineral Carbonation
column6:
The proposed project is the fusion of two approved capsule proposal entitled, °Self-Supporting Zeolite-Activated Biochar Composites
with Hierarchical Porosity for CO2 Capture ° and °Carbon Sequestration through Mineral Carbonation of Scrubbed CO2 in a Fluidized
Bed Reactor". The combined proposal is a sequential approach to capturing CO2 using self-supporting zeolite composites made from
zeolite-activated biochar with hierarchical porosity, followed by the conversion of scrubbed CO2 to mineral carbonates through a
fluidized bed granulation process.
To create the composites, zeolite is grown within a geopolymer matrix, acting as a scaffold. Activated biochar, derived from agricultural
waste, is incorporated to improve the composite's material properties. Hierarchical porosity is achieved using foaming techniques.
BET equipment will be used to conduct CO2 adsorption isotherm and kinetic studies to assess the performance of the composites.
Given the unique properties of the self-supporting zeolite-activated blochar composite in adsorbing CO2, the process is expected to
concentrate the CO2 in the inlet gas of the scrubber. The scrubber operates by absorbing CO2 through chemisorption with the aid of
an alkali solution. Scrubbed CO2, in the form of carbonate ions, is combined with either magnesium or calcium ions in a fluidized-bed
granulator to obtain granules of mineral carbonates with high purity and low moisture content Monitoring and process control will
be included in the project to automate both laboratory and pilot-scale integrated system.

column4: Water Resources Assessment: Flood Resilience and Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to Address Water Security Issues in Pasig-Marikina and Laguna Lake Basin
column6: Water insecurity results from the socio-environmental changes and exposure of water systems to different hazards. The provision of ecosystem services for water supply is impacted by multiple factors including high economic activities, population growth, deforestation, and land conversion aggravated by countrywide flood and water scarcity risks due to changes in rainfall distributions. This study addresses water security issues by assessing water resources for industrial, agricultural, and domestic sectors in the Pasig-Marikina and Laguna Lake basin. The project will use risk-based approaches to comprehensively evaluate conditions that expose water resource systems and their management to hazards and their responses and capacity to recover from probable impacts. This will include an assessment of water resources' sectoral resilience for water quantity through water resource accounting for demand-supply gap analysis, and contamination hotspot mapping and water quality assessment. The results of water security vulnerability and risk assessments can provide a basis to increase the resilience of water systems through Nature-based Solution (NbS) options and Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) recommendations. Integrating NbS and IWRM principles fosters a multi-faceted approach to addressing the identified issues and ensures stakeholder participation across sectors.

column4: BIG TICKET PROGRAM: Biologics in Pharma
column6:
"Biologics, or biological products, include a wide array of products such as vaccines, blood and blood components, recombinant therapeutic proteins, monoclonal antibodies, and cell therapies. They represent a rapidly growing segment of the pharmaceutical industry with significant potential to address unmet medical needs. Compared to small molecule drugs that are usually chemically synthesized, biologics are derived from a variety of natural sources such as humans, animals and microorganisms. While this makes biologics more complex, they also offer the potential for more targeted and/or safer treatment options, and even treating diseases which were once considered impossible or difficult to treat. DOST through its programs on health specifically on drug discovery and development, omic technologies, and re-emerging and emerging diseases have laid initial groundwork for local capacity building and R&D aimed at exploring biologics.
This program aims to capitalize on these initial efforts thus far, and further improve and increase investment in R&D for biologics to enhance our capabilities in biotechnology, support the development of innovative therapies, and improve public health outcomes particularly in providing precise and personalized treatments.
This initiative will foster collaboration between academia, industry, and healthcare providers, and accelerate the translation of research into clinical applications."

column4: Water and Air Profiling and Wastewater Treatment of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) from select areas of Water and Pollution Sources Within Luzon
column6:
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are chemicals widely used in consumer products that pose a threat
to the environment, mostly in water systems, and to human health due to their ubiquitous nature. PFAS
contamination poses a high risk due to their bioaccumulation, persistence, and potential toxic effects. PFAS
decontamination methods are limited and not well studied; some have been ineffective due to insufficient data,
inadequate monitoring, and a lack of comprehensive policies.
Metabolomics is the study of a large number of small-molecule metabolites within a system, and metabolomics
analysis can be used to investigate the metabolite composition of water, and identify PFAS. The project aims to
characterize biomass, air, and water samples collected from specific water bodies in the Philippines through
untargeted LC-HRMS-Orbitrap. Observed PFAS content would then be quantified through GC-MS. In addition,
treatment methodologies for PFAS-contaminated water samples will be tested and assessed through targeted
PFAS analysis using LC-MS-QTOF.
This project involves the collaboration of researchers from academia and industry. We will be working together
to translate the findings on PFAS contamination and treatment into viable technologies for use in the treatment
plants. The data collected from the metabolomics studies will also be used to guide the creation of policies,
surveillance, and protocols for PFAS. Appropriate surveillance and treatment policies on PFAS monitoring and
protocols on PFAS decontamination will help ensure the preservation of the environment and human health

column4: Integrating Spirituality as a Core Subject in Philippine State Universities: A Framework for Maka-Diyos Education toward Peace and Nation-Building
column6:
This project seeks to develop, pilot-test, and institutionalize Spirituality as a core subject in state universities, grounded in the national values articulated in the motto Maka-Diyos, Makatao, Makakalikasan, at Makabansa. It is premised on the growing recognition that spirituality—understood as the human pursuit of meaning, transcendence, and interconnectedness—is a powerful yet delicate force. When nurtured responsibly, it serves as a catalyst for integrity, peacebuilding, and national development; when distorted or exploited, it can fuel division, extremism, and moral decline.

In higher education, spirituality is often marginalized or deliberately avoided, creating a critical vacuum. This absence allows false ideologies, pseudo-religious movements, and ethical indifference to proliferate, undermining social cohesion and weakening the moral foundations of democracy and peace. Addressing this gap, the project will design a values-based, non-sectarian curriculum and teaching modules on spirituality as a core subject, aimed at forming reflective, ethically grounded, and peace-oriented citizens.

A defining feature of the initiative is its interfaith and intercultural approach. Curriculum development will engage religious leaders, scholars, and cultural practitioners from diverse traditions—including Christianity, Islam, Indigenous Spiritualities, Buddhism, and others—to identify shared moral values and spiritual principles that promote compassion, justice, and respect for diversity. The curriculum will incorporate a comparative study of major belief systems, enabling students to appreciate both common ethical foundations and distinct spiritual perspectives.

Through this inclusive and dialogical framework, the project advances spiritual literacy, equipping students with the capacity for critical yet respectful engagement on questions of faith, meaning, and moral responsibility. It strengthens resilience against extremism and ideological manipulation, while fostering social cohesion, peace, and sustainable development.

The project is also responsive to ongoing national discussions on the rationalization of the General Education Curriculum (GEC). While supporting efforts to decongest degree programs, it proposes a principled consolidation into four enduring core subjects aligned with the national values: Maka-Diyos, Makatao, Makakalikasan, at Makabansa. In this framework, Ethics represents Makatao; Rizal and NSTP—mandated by law—represent Makabansa; and environmental education initiatives represent Makakalikasan. This proposal focuses on developing the Maka-Diyos component—the currently missing moral-spiritual dimension—thereby completing a coherent, four-pillared framework for holistic higher education.

The console shall be capable of collecting and storing sensitive data and deriving meaningful value from it through the use of advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence. column4: Innovative Wood Processing Techniques: Utilizing Thermally Modified Philippine Industrial Tree Plantation Species in High Value-Furniture Application
column6: This research aims to enhance wood processing in the Philippines by optimizing thermal modification (TM) and hybrid lamination for industrial tree plantation species (ITPS), specifically Falcataria moluccana (Falcata), Swietenia macrophylla (Mahogany), Acacia mangium (Mangium), and Gmelina arborea (Gmelina). While Falcata and Mangium are widely used in plywood, crates, and pallets, and Mahogany and Gmelina in furniture and construction, their durability, dimensional stability, and aesthetic properties require improvement for high-value applications. This study will (1) characterize the physico-mechanical properties of thermally-modified ITPS wood, (2) assess the effects of TM on stability, durability, and color transformation, (3) determine optimal lay-up configurations for hybrid laminated composites, and (4) develop processing parameters for prototype production. Thermal modification enhances resistance to decay fungi and wood-boring insects while altering color to resemble premium hardwoods. Hybrid lamination strengthens structural integrity and expands design possibilities. The findings will support the production of high-quality, all-wood or mixed-media furniture utilizing thermally modified ITPS. By integrating these innovative techniques, this study aims to improve ITPS based products' market competitiveness, promote sustainable wood utilization, and contribute to the growth of the Philippine furniture industry.

column4: Test Application of Air Classification Technology for Plant Proteins, Starches and Fibers from Philippine Mung Bean as Food Ingredients

The country has yet to produce its own supply of plant component ingredients using indigenous raw materials to meet the rising demand for sustainable plant-based processed food. Traditional wet chemical extraction of plant proteins, starches, and fibers also has negative environmental implications because this method uses large amounts of energy, water, and chemicals. Research on the extraction of these components has shifted to dry physical methods like air classification that can separate particles based on size and density while using less energy and water.

column4: Radiation Treatment of Emerging pollutants in Used water (RE-Used)
column6:
Re-using treated water from wastewater treatment facilities to augment water supply is becoming more relevant due to the depletion and pollution of freshwater sources such as dams, rivers, and lakes and an increasing water demand both for
industrial and domestic use. However, lack of affordable technologies capable of removing emerging pollutants prevents establishments generating these pollutants from re-using their used water. In the hospitals surveyed by the partner company,
Anthroserv Inc., hospital wastewater contains around 40% non-biodegradable pollutants. While Anthroserv Inc. desires to provide wastewater management solutions to this segment, their existing technology based on biological treatment is only suitable for wastewater with low percentage of non-biodegradable pollutants. This means that they are not yet capable to provide a treatment technology to make these potential clients comply with DENR effluent standards. A tertiary method for removing non-biodegrabable components is thus necessary.

With the goal of providing a cost-effective technology for used water treatment not only by removal, but by degradation and mineralization of non-biodegradable pollutants, this project proposes to demonstrate the feasibility of electron beam radiation treatment of hospital wastewater and develop a demonstration facility to facilitate R&D, capacity building, and local adoption of the e-beam wastewater treatment technology.

As one of the most common causes of foodborne illnesses in many

undertaken by relevant national government authorities. Most of the
literature on the surveillance on occurrence and outbreaks caused by L.
monocytogenes were from European countries and the USA (Rakhmawati
et al., 2013) and minimal in developing countries such as the Philippines.
While listeriosis is a rare infection, it has a high fatality rate in specific
population groups (pregnant and immuno-compromised individuals). This
premise places L. monocytogenes as one of the top pathogens contributing

The results of this study will contribute to the microbiological risk
assessment by providing prevalence and levels of L. monocytogenes in

column4: Nanofiller-Enhanced Cassava Starch/Carrageenan Composite Films and Coatings for High-Strength and Heat Sealable Food Packaging
column6:
Petrochemical-based plastics, though cost-effective and widely used in packaging, are criticized for their environmental impact and non- biodegradability. In contrast, natural polymer films offer a sustainable alternative
This project aims to investigate the development of natural polymer films and coating from cassava starch/carrageenan composite with cross-linking agents and reinforced with nanofillers for sustainable heat-sealable materials in food. The commercial cassava starch will be used and carrageenan will be sourced from a partner in Tawi-Tawi. A sample preparation process of natural polymer coating was done through dissolving nanofillers, cassava starch and carrageenan in deionized water at 85°C for 30 minutes, adding glycerol as a plasticizer, and drying the mixtures in an oven at 100°C for 24 hours. A control film of pure cassava starch was also prepared.
The films were cut into dumbbell shapes and tested for tensile strength using a universal testing machine. The film with 80% cassava starch and 20% Carrageenan (C80G20) demonstrated the highest tensile strength at 16.38 MPa, indicating an optimal blend ratio for enhanced mechanical properties. Films with higher carrageenan content exhibited reduced tensile strength, likely due to poor adhesion and excessive plasticizing effects. This research highlights the potential of cassava starch/carrageenan composites with cross linking agents and different nanofillers in creating strong, flexible, and sustainable packaging materials.

column4: Microplastic Capture through Electrostatically-Assisted Silica-Modified Substrate: A Novel Environmental Mitigation Approach to Microplastic Pollution (MicroCapture)
column6: The proposed research initiative is critically important given the escalating threat of microplastic contamination in the Taguibo River, a vital source of drinking water for Butuan City. The presence of microplastics in both water and sediment poses significant risks to public health and environmental integrity, necessitating urgent action to develop effective remediation methods. The adoption of MicroCapture technology, specifically designed for point-of-use application at the household level, represents a transformative approach. By leveraging the electrostatic properties of silica-modified substrate, this innovative solution significantly enhances the capture efficiency of microplastics, filling a crucial gap in existing remediation strategies. Beyond pollution reduction, MicroCapture fosters scientific innovation and technological advancement, promising not only to safeguard water potability but also to catalyze economic and environmental benefits. The potential for cost-effective microplastic remediation underscores the timely importance of this research, marking it as a pivotal investment in advancing environmental sustainability and protecting public health

column4: Machine Learning Interatomic Potential for High Entropy Alloys
column6: High entropy alloys (HEA), which are multicomponent alloys, are referred to as the next-generation alloys due to their better properties compared to conventional alloys. Understanding their behavior requires the investigation at the atomic scale level which necessitates an accurate interatomic potential. This research project will generate accurate interatomic potential based on machine learning for HEAs. Different computational materials science methods combined with materials informatics methods will be performed to generate the interatomic potential. The results of the simulations will be compared with experimental findings not only to validate the accuracy of the generated potential but also to provide insights from computational materials science point of view.

column4: Intelligate: Modernizing Milkfish Tidal Pond Gating System and Water Monitoring System Through Smart Aquaculture Technologies
column6: Since the advent of the tidal brackishwater pond operations in the Philippine Aquaculture scene, little to no advancement, innovation and development were seen in terms of pond engineering, design, and creation. The traditional method of managing water in tidal brackishwater ponds has remained its operations unchanged and not developed from its introduction up until this very day. This traditional practice has become increasingly unsustainable, utilizing wooden planks which are becoming scarce and expensive. These flashboards are highly susceptible to degradation due to prolonged exposure to seawater and varying weather conditions. Moreover, this current practice is labor intensive as it requires manual opening and closing of the gates, as well as a need for the farm caretakers to stay up late to wait for the tidal change. It is also worth highlighting that the underdevelopment and lack of innovation of the old aquaculture practices has remained to be one of the main hindrances in the increase of the Aquaculture Industry production. The Maria’s Village and Aqua Farm, an aquaculture farm based in Roxas City, Capiz, owned by Mr. Graciano Panaguiton, Vice-Chairman of Panay Aqua Farmers Consumers Cooperative, faced similar issue in his fishponds. DOST-MIRDC stood up to the challenge and answered the call, thus, the creation of this research proposal. The current proposed research study aims to develop sustainable and automated water control gate operation utilizing HDPE plastic as a flashboard material and water level sensors targeting the pond’s main gate replacing the existing wooden flashboards, and incorporation of automated water parameter monitoring system for ease of operations and rearing monitoring.

column4: Integration of Paper Waste-Derived Nanocrystalline Cellulose with Banana Pseudo Stem Fiber as Sustainable and Biodegradable Foam (Nanafoam) for Cold Chain Storage
column6:
Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) is one of the most common materials used for a variety of purposes from industrial setup to household materials. In 2018, the EPS global market amounted to 7,992.8 kilotons and was estimated to be around 10,000 kilotons by 2023 (The Global Expanded Polystyrene Market, Industry Size Forecast, n.d.). However, EPS is a microplastic which is essentially non- biodegradable as it takes hundreds of years to decompose (Meiffren-Swango, 2022). Combining it with being lightweight, easily broken down and dispersed, it contributes significantly to microplastic pollutants across all ecosystems (Global Seafood Alliance, 2022).
EPS has been extensively used as packaging for cold chain storage due to its capacity for thermal insulation, including biomedical packaging. It is, therefore, imperative to find alternative solutions or material to EPS. In this project, nanocrystalline cellulose (NCC) extracted from paper waste and banana pseudo stem (BPS) fiber pulp will be used to create an EPS alternative foam for biomedical cold chain packaging. NCC and BPS are biodegradable and abundant wastes, making them sustainable. Integrating NCC and BPS therefore can eliminate the huge environmental hazard and pollution that EPS brings, and further adds the benefit of reducing unutilized wastes.

column4: Integrated Rapid Ionomics and Predictive Modeling for Smarter Nutrient Management in Sugarcane (iCanePredict)
column6:
The Philippines sugarcane industry significantly contributes to the economy, generating approximately ₱70Billion annually. However, due to intensive crop production and monocropping practices, most sugarcane farmlands in the country degraded and become less productive. This has led to challenges in achieving the potential yield, primarily due to high nutrient requirements of high-yielding sugarcane cultivars and high cost of commercial fertilizers. generalized nutrient recommendation and inefficient fertilizer application have further aggravated the problem of farmland productivity. 

Thus, there is a pressing need to reevaluate and redesign the current crop cultural management system and practices to boost production if not sustain the country's sugarcane industry. Effective management of nutrients plays a crucial role in enhancing efficiency and productivity. Recent studies conducted by DOST-PNRI in collaboration with Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) have shown the limited response of sugarcane to NPK fertilization, emphasizing the importance of examining the nutrient balance between macronutrients and micronutrients

Modern analytical techniques such as rapid ionomics through high throughput multi-elemental profiling, sophisticated decision-support systems (DSS) and nutrient predictive modeling can fully exploit the yield potential of high-yielding sugarcane cultivars. Nutrient predictive models have been widely used for crop nutrient management and monitoring of nutritional status in different crops such as banana, pineapple, rice, potatoes, coffee, mango, corn, soybean and sugarcane. With the Department of Agriculture (DA) and Sugar Industry Development Act (SIDA) implementation supporting the upgrading the soil laboratories in the country with advanced analytical equipment (e.g. XRF, AAS, CNS analyzer, ICP-OES) capable of multi-elemental determinations, the implementation of rapid ionomics, nutrient predictive models and DSS for monitoring sugarcane nutrition is highly feasible and timely.

By venturing into smart and high performance finishing for now-woven textiles, the capabilities and functions of nonwoven textiles will expand for new applications. column4: Geochronology and Isotope Geochemistry of Philippine Sea Ocean Floor and Onshore Analogues: Implications for the Early Tectonic History of the Philippine Sea Plate
column6: The forthcoming establishment of the National Isotope Center provides a nexus for integrating the nuclear analytical and isotopic capabilities of the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute. The scheduled installation of a triple quadruple inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer coupled with a laser ablation system at PNRI in the next two (2) years will result in the expansion of maximum determinable ages from thousand years to geological timescales in millions of years, and to higher, more robust closure temperatures. With this capability, whole-rock geochemistry, U-Pb ages, and Sr-Nd-Pb(-Hf) isotopic compositions of Cretaceous Philippine ophiolites, as onshore analogues of the Philippine Sea plate ocean floor, will be determined to characterize their mantle domain boundaries through time, and elucidate the early tectonic history of the Philippine Sea plate. Because the Philippines does not have an active ocean floor research program, initiation of collaborative work in the Philippine Sea plate with Japanese counterparts may lead to opportunities to sample ocean floor of surrounding marginal basins.

column4: Establishing the Use of Spent Coconut Kernel as Renewable Source of High-Value Bioactive Mannan-derived Compounds using Radiation
column6: Large amounts of agro-industrial residues are generated during commercial processing of various crops. The Philippines generates megatons of agro-industrial residues annually from sugarcane, rice, coconut, com, etc. Considering the likely increase in the generation of agro-industrial residues owing to the surge in demand for crops, strategies should be improved to address the issue of waste disposal and utilize the agro-industrial residues efficiently as a source of high-value materials, such as bioactive compounds, which have wide applications in food and medicine. Ionizing radiation has proven to increase the extraction yield and properties of bioactive compounds from agro-industrial residues. Radiation technologies offer eco-friendly research tools that are becoming a solution for many countries in developing novel approaches. This study will adopt and improve radiation-aided methods to develop a postharvest production system for the recovery of D-mannose from coconut meat residues. D-Mannose is a highly marketable product that generated a global revenue of US$830.8 Mn in 2023. We envision the study to provide science-based support for establishing a local industry on D-mannose production from agro-industrial residues through radiation-assisted technology, which will promote sustainable competency of the coconut industry and give access to this high-value niche market providing additional income to locals.

column4: Development of FPRDI Hybrid Barrel and Its Impact on the Ageing of Local Wine and Spirit

To fully participate in the global trend, Filipino beverage makers must develop innovative and new products. One approach involves the development of beverages from local sources. column4: Development of a Sustainable Process for Functionalized Biochar Synthesis Enabling Platform Chemicals from Local Biomass (BIOCHARM)
column6: The study begins with selecting bifunctional biochar catalysts (BIOCHARM-1) with Lewis and Brřnsted acid sites based on fructose and glucose conversion to 5-HMF. Optimization studies will refine 5-HMF synthesis conditions, considering solvent type, catalyst loading, temperature, and reaction time. The optimized process will then be applied to whole lignocellulosic biomass, comparing BIOCHARM-1 with conventional catalysts. Regeneration and recycling of spent BIOCHARM-1, along with 5-HMF purification using organic solvents and distillation, will also be explored. 5-HMF will be converted into EL using BIOCHARM-2, a Brřnsted acid-functionalized catalyst optimized through different biochar activation conditions. By utilizing local agricultural residues, this project advances biochar-based catalysis for platform chemical production, addressing key research gaps in the Philippines. It aligns with circular economy principles,  positioning the country as a leader in sustainable chemical manufacturing while contributing to the global bioeconomy.

column4: Development and Safety Evaluation of Natural UV Filters from Philippine Agricultural Byproducts for Cosmetics Application
column6:
The Philippines has abundant agricultural resources, yet agricultural byproducts such as sugarcane bagasse and spent coffee grounds contribute to significant environmental challenges. Simultaneously, the cosmetic industry struggles to source sustainable raw materials, often relying on imports. More so, chemical sunscreen agents also present limitations and adverse effects, increasing the demand for plant-based alternatives that complement natural minerals in sun protection. Hence, this project aims to develop natural UV filters from agricultural byproducts by extracting compounds from sugarcane bagasse and spent coffee grounds, which will be encapsulated to enhance stability. These bioactive ingredients will serve as sustainable, eco-friendly UV filters in cosmetic products like shampoos, serums, and sunscreens, offering an alternative to synthetic filters and booster to physical sunscreen agents. 

Additionally, skin sensitization remains a critical concern in cosmetics, highlighting the need for thorough safety evaluations. The DOST ITDI's Standards and Testing Division faces challenges in conducting skin sensitization testing due to limited availablity of guinea pigs for animal-based testing and the prohibitive costs involved. To address this, the project will validate the Epidermal Sensitization Assay method, a non-animal alternative using reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) models. This method has shown high human relevance for assessing skin sensitization in emerging studies, as compared with other in vitro methods under OECD TG 4222D.

By providing sustainable, plant-based UV filters and enhancing DOST ITDI's capacity for ethical, reliable skin sensitization testing, this project aligns with global trends toward natural, eco-friendly cosmetic formulations and nonanimal testing. It offers the cosmetic industry an opportunity to innovate with safer, greener ingredients while addressing pressing environmental and ethical concerns.

column4: Development and Application of Rapid, Non-destructive Heavy Metal and Trace Element Detection Techniques in Plant Materials
column6:
The safety and quality control of agricultural products, including coconut, mango, banana, cacao, coffee, corn, cabbage, and lettuce are crucial not only for protecting consumers but also for building consumer trust and enhancing competitiveness in both local and international markets. The monitoring of heavy metals and trace elements, including essential nutrients as well as dangerous heavy metals is a necessary step to achieve food safety regulations and crop quality standards. The Philippines faces difficulties in trace element analysis because the country lacks sufficient advanced laboratories that perform MP-AES, GFAAS, ICP-MS, ICP-OES, and other related methods. The conventional methods used for these tests are expensive nd time-consuming and require hazardous reagents and skilled personnel who are scarce in many rural and regional areas.

The development of rapid, nondestructive analytical technologies such as X-ray flourescence (XRF)  and laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) provides an applicable solution to this problem because they are portable and scalable. The technique enables detection of multiple elements through direct analysis which needs either no or minimal sample preparation. The technology produces fast results through real-time operations while operating without chemical reagents, which results in safer, faster and less expensive testing compared to traditional approaches. The portable nature of XRF and LIBS technology along with user-friendly operation enables field-level deployment, thus extending accurate elemental analysis capabilities throughout the nation.

column4: Determining Laboratory Competency by Interlaboratory Comparison Scheme Using Locally Developed Proficiency Test Items for Dairy Product
column6: The project proposal, Determining Laboratory Competency by Interlaboratory Comparison Scheme Using Locally Developed Proficiency Items for Dairy Products , was conceptualize to provide assistance to the local microbiological laboratories by developing proficiency test (PT) materials and providing PT schemes. As part of the food production cycle, laboratory testing is an integral component in ensuring food safety through accurate measurements. Through the National Metrology Laboratory (NML), the Department of Science and Technology – Industrial Technology Development Institute (DOST – ITDI) is continuously developing its capability in the field of biological metrology for microbiological measurements. This was initiated in response for the need for a local PT provider in the country. In support of ensuring food safety and product quality, the NML has initially focused its activities for the seafood industry and developed PT materials and provided PT schemes on Salmonella sp. Detection, Aerobic Plate Count (APC) in milkfish and octopus, and Total Coliform Count and E. coli Count in milkfish. For this proposal, the NML will expand its services for the dairy industry by developing the PT materials Salmonella sp. Detection, APC, Total Coliform Count and E. coli Count in powered milk. This will be followed by PT schemes to be participated in by local laboratories as part of their quality assurance program.

column4: Determination of Emerging Contaminants Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) and Mineral Oil Hydrocarbons (MOH) in Food
column6:
This project will focus on the development and validation of test methods for the analysis of food contaminants that are of global concern such per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and mineral oil hydrocarbons (mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons or MOAH and mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons or MOSH). These contaminants pose safety and health risks to consumers hence their presence in food products need to be monitored using chemical testing methods that are recognized in the scientific community.

The test methods will be based on international references such as the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), Official Methods of Analysis of AOAC International, US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and EU Reference Laboratories. After validation, the methods will be applied for the expansion of the Chemistry Laboratory's ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation with DTI-Philippine Accreditation Bureau and DOH-FDA, and seek recognition from Department of Agriculture attached agencies. These methods will be part of DOSTITDI's routine testing services for the public.

The project will also aim to harmonize the test methods in the country which is aligned with the AOAC Southeast Asia laboratories through provision of training to other laboratories on the validated methods. By enhancing the testing capability of our laboratories, we will be able to support the government's effort in strengthening the food safety regulatory network and protect the consumers. Moreover, data from testing of various food samples may be used for risk assessment studies

column4: Detection of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes (ARGs) in Aquacultured Whiteleg Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) in Western Visayas and its Implication on Food Safety
column6: Concomitant with the rise in antibiotic use in aquaculture, there has been an emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among bacterial fish pathogens. Cultured shrimp are reported to contain antimicrobial resistance pathogens. If shrimp that harbor resistant bacteria with AMR genes end up being consumed, these many pose health risk through the possible transfer of antibiotic-resistant bacteria from shrimp to humans or the uptake of the antimcirobial resistant genes (ARGs) of the host microbiota through transformation. Due to the significance and undesirable effects of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes in food safety, the proposed study will be conducted over a period of 24 months and aims to create a profile of antimicrobial resistance genes from the cultures whiteleg shrimp from various farms in Western Visayas.

column4: Design and Development of Capacitance Wood Moisture Meter for Wood and Non-Wood Forests Products
column6: The industry has expressed a clear need for an advanced moisture meter that extends the MC measurement range up to 100% and incorporates non-destructive techniques. The absence of locally calibrated, non-destructive moisture meters exacerbates the challenges faced by wood and NTFP processors in the Philippines, as imported options are often costly and not specifically tailored to the properties of local species. To address these needs, this project proposes the development of a new capacitance moisture meter (FA 507 Type II). This advanced meter will overcome the limitations of the current FA 507 by providing accurate, non-destructive MC measurements across a broad range (6% to 100%). The new meter will be specifically calibrated for commercially used and exported species, including both wood and non-timber forest products like bamboo, vines, and rattan, offering a more affordable, precise, and user-friendly alternative to existing technologies. By implementing this innovative solution, local industries will benefit from enhanced product quality and reduced operational costs. This development will also preserve the appearance and value of both wood and non-wood forest products, supporting the growth and sustainability of the Philippine forestry sector.

column4: Data Driven Framework for Powder Production and Additive Manufacturing of Cobalt-less Maraging Steel Alloy System
column6:
The Additive Manufacturing Center (AMCEN) and Materials Development (MATDEV) Laboratory are actively working towards expanding their initiatives as outlined in the Additive Manufacturing S&T Long Term R&D Plan. One significant challenge to the widespread adoption of additive manufacturing (AM) in the Philippines is the limited and expensive supply of materials, such as polymers, metals, and ceramics, available for prototyping and fabrication. 

Additionally, studies focusing on metal AM are constrained by the high cost of raw materials and the lack of local suppliers. To address this gap, the proposed project involves collaboration among experts from DOST-ITDI, DOSTMIRDC, UP DMMME, UPLB, and Mapua University. This initiative is guided by Dr. Rigoberto Advincula of the University of Tennessee Knoxville, USA and Dr. Clodualdo Aranas, Jr., a Balik Scientist and Metal Additive Manufacturing expert from the University of New Brunswick, Canada. The project aims to develop and optimize process parameters such as alloy composition, atomization, etc. for local metal powder production for metal additive manufacturing (AM) while leveraging AI/ML technologies to reduce production costs and promote the adoption of AM technology within the local mold and die industries. By localizing the production of metal alloys, the project will effectively reduce the raw material cost for powder-based AM feedstock, alongside other benefits such as reduced lead time, costs, importation, and wastage. This will benefit companies like ADVANTEK who are exploring ways to design and utilize efficient cooling channels customized to their needs through metal additive manufacturing. 

The success of the project will lead to higher adoption of metal AM, consistent with the needs outlined in the Metals and Engineering Sector Roadmap, particularly in the Tool and Die, Metal Casting, and Machining and Fabrication sectors.

column4: Bioconversion of Crude Glycerol into Value-added Compounds
column6: The abundance of crude glycerol generated by the biodiesel industry is a challenge that must be addressed. Although crude glycerol is used as a feedstock for products such as animal feeds, polyurethane, and biogas, its current usage cannot decrease the surplus. This “waste” product presents a great potential for further production of value-added chemicals such as 1,3- propanediol (1,3-PD), specialty lipids, and biosurfactant. These chemicals can be synthesized by microorganisms, and glycerol could serve as a carbon source in the fermentation process. Crude glycerol, however, is contaminated with methanol, soap, and other impurities which may inhibit microbial growth. Suitable and efficient purification methods are necessary prior to fermentation. Utilization of robust and generally-regarded-as-safe (GRAS) microbial systems to produce value-added compounds from crude glycerol presents a more cost-effective, sustainable, and environmentally friendly process. This project aims to devise a “green” purification method for crude glycerol and to discover and develop microbial systems for the production of 1,3-PD, lipids, and biosurfactant in aid to a sustainable circular bioeconomy

column4: ASCal: An Automated System for the Calibration of Handheld Digital Multimeters (DMM)
column6: Calibration laboratories play a critical role in ensuring the accuracy and reliability of measurement instruments across various industries. Currently, there are more than 50 accredited calibration and testing laboratories all over the country according to the data published on the website of the Philippines Accreditation Bureau. Furthermore, calibration is essential across industries like manufacturing, healthcare, trade, and environmental monitoring, ensuring accurate measurements for quality assurance, regulatory compliance, and fair-trade practices. Hence, it has been compromised by the fact that the calibration process is still done manually. Sonju Engineering Services is one of the companies that still practice manual calibration. It consumes most of their operators' time and effort as manual calibration is time-consuming, fatiguing, and difficult to collect data. On that note, the need for automation in calibration systems arises. With the advancements in technology, there is a growing demand for automated calibration systems to improve efficiency, accuracy, and consistency in calibration processes. Applying automation in calibration can resolve the limitations of manual calibration systems such as reducing time, easy in collecting data, and autopilot measurement. By verifying the accuracy and reliability of measurement instruments, calibration enables businesses to maintain product quality, adhere to regulations, and foster fair transactions.

TOWARDS A SUSTAINABLE PHILIPPINE FOOD SYSTEM: UNDERSTANDING AVAILABILITY, ACCESSIBILITY, LIVED EXPERIENCES AND NUTRITION OUTCOMES THROUGH MAPPING AND MODELLING GEOSPATIAL AND OBSERVATIONAL DATA (PALIGID): Project 1. Survey on the Food Environment Towards Sustainable Food Production and Consumption (SARI)
column6: The food system encompasses interconnected activities from production to consumption and disposal. (Cohen, 2019). The current unsustainable practices within this system promote calorie-dense, nutrient-poor foods, leading to malnutrition, obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases (Hawkes, 2018). An unsustainable food system also contributes to environmental degradation, food insecurity, and health disparities (FAO, 2020). There is a strained public health system and economic stability due to the dual burden of undernutrition and obesity (Popkin, 2020). The country is beset by the triple burden of undernutrition, overnutrition, and micronutrient deficiencies. There is a general lack of diversity in the diet, inadequate intake of energy and key micronutrients, and widespread food insecurity (DOST-FNRI, 2022). It is noted that food systems research often focuses on isolated components, potentially leading to mismatches in production and unmet demand for affordable, nutritious foods (Marshall et al., 2021; Cohen, 2019). Various organizations in the country have taken steps toward improving food production, better consumption, and nutrition, but in silos. This study, aims to analyze the interrelationships of the food environment, food consumption, and food value chains to support healthy, affordable, and sustainable diets for all Filipinos and to provide more context-specific strategies to address the gaps in the food system.

column4: THE SIBUYAN SEA SYMPHONY (SSS): EXPLORING PELAGIC ECOSYSTEMS AND FISHERIES DYNAMICS: Project 3. Fisheries and Feeding Ecology of the Pelagic Resources in the Sibuyan Sea (FiFE)
column6: One obstacle in understanding and managing fisheries is the lack of basic information on catches, fishing effort, fishing grounds, and biological information. The Sibuyan Sea, which includes the Romblon Group of Islands - Tablas, Romblon, and Sibuyan islands, is a productive marine ecosystem supporting diverse fisheries such as small pelagics, demersal fishes, and shrimp species (Lumayno et al., 2023; Gonzales et al., 2021; Rada et al., 2019; Philbrick, 1987). Yet, despite its significance to the fishing industry, the Sibuyan Sea received little research attention compared to other fishing grounds, such as the Visayan and Sulu Seas. Thus, the fisheries catch estimate, and the current fishing condition remains poorly understood. This project will conduct fisheries profiling, monitor daily catch and effort, and fishing ground information of target pelagic species and gears, and collect subsample of catches for biological studies. i.e., feeding ecology. The results from this project can be used as a basis in determining catch and effort estimates, seasonality of catches, important fishing grounds information, annual catch estimates, fishing calendar, food availability, and well-being of fish stocks in the Sibuyan Sea. Consequently, these results can be used in crafting science-based guidelines to conserve and ensure the sustainability of important fishing grounds and pelagic resources in the Sibuyan Sea.

column4: THE SIBUYAN SEA SYMPHONY (SSS): EXPLORING PELAGIC ECOSYSTEMS AND FISHERIES DYNAMICS: Project 2. Biological Assessment of Sibuyan Stocks (BASS): Insights on Population Dynamics and Reproduction for Sustainable Fisheries
column6: This project, part of the proposed research program, "The Sibuyan Sea Symphony (SSS)," aims to study the population dynamics and reproductive biology of key small pelagic fish species in the Sibuyan Sea, an ecologically important but understudied area in the central Philippines. the project will focus on  key parameters such as growth, recruitment, mortality, exploitation rates, gonadal development, spawning seasonality, and fecundity. Given the limited scientific data available for the Sibuyan Sea, this project seeks to fill critical knowledge gaps by producing baseline biological information for the region's pelagic fisheries. Finding will be compared with data from other regions to inform science-based strategies for sustainable fisheries management, contributing to food security, livelihoods, and marine biodiversity conservation.

column4: THE SIBUYAN SEA SYMPHONY (SSS): EXPLORING PELAGIC ECOSYSTEMS AND FISHERIES DYNAMICS: Project 1. Dynamics Regulating Underwater Marine Systems (DRUMS): Oceanography, Biodiversity, and Productivity of the Sibuyan Sea
column6:
While oceanographic studies in the Visayan Sea are abundant (i.e., Visayan Sea Modelling for Operational Oceanography (VISMO)), the research efforts in the Sibuyan Sea remain limited. Since the hydrographic information on the Sibuyan Sea is currently scarce, satellite data is expected to reveal hydrographic phenomena, i.e., gyre or eddy formation, that may influence the fine-scale circulation in this region. Multiparameter, ADCP, and CTD measurements, and water chemical analyses around the study site will provide a more detailed picture of the hydrography and its influence to the supply of organic and inorganic materials in the region. With periodic on-board expeditions around these small, isolated islands in the Sibuyan Sea, the seasonality of hydrographic, chemical, and biological parameters may be revealed. This information will be correlated with the diversity and abundance of zooplankton, not only to show the complex interplay of physico-chemical and biological processes, but also to hone in to their importance as the key driver of fisheries productivity.

With the continuous exploitation of fishery resources, the fishery stocks in the SSS and around small islands may be perceived to be at the brink of collapse. Hence, there is a pressing need for a thorough ecosystem-based research approach to understand how these resources are sustained in their natural habitat despite the threats of destructive fishing practices, especially if they do not appear to be peripherally depleted. This study will provide science-based data for informed policy making decisions related to fishery management and conservation. It is interesting to explore the influence of shallow sills and small island-induced hydrographic processes and how they impact productivity enhancement in the Philippines, an archipelago of 7,640 islands, with fisheries as a main source of livelihood among its citizenry.

column4: SEVEN LAKES ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING PROGRAM: STRATEGIES TOWARD SUSTAINABLE LAKE ECOSYSTEM (7 LAMPS) - PHASE 2: Project 4. Endocrine Disruption Responses in Fish Near Outfalls Sewers in the Lakes of San Pablo
column6:
Local studies have shown evidence of the effects of endocrine disrupting compounds (EDCs) in freshwater fish from aquaculture areas in Laguna de Bay and
from the seven lakes of San Pablo. Endocrine disruption has not only been documented in vertebrate organisms such as fish. Its occurrence in invertebrate organisms has also been reported. The potential adverse health effects of EDCs necessitate the formulation of measures that will aim to reduce or minimize its discharge into the environment, and consequently, its impact on vulnerable organisms such as fish. A step towards the realization of this goal is the identification of point sources of endocrine disruptors and their contribution to the
responses observed in fish. This study aims to determine endocrine disruption responses of caged Nile tilapia in relation to levels of endocrine disrupting compounds at sites close to municipal outfall sewers in Bunot, Palakpakin, Sampaloc and Yambo Lakes, and to determine seasonal variation in the degree of biological responses in caged fish and
EDC concentration in water samples.

column4: SEVEN LAKES ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING PROGRAM: STRATEGIES TOWARD SUSTAINABLE LAKE ECOSYSTEM (7 LAMPS) - PHASE 2: Project 2. Development and Valuation of Sustainable Land-and-Lake-Use Plans Using Participatory Watershed Land-and-Lake-Use Management (PWLLM) Approach in Lakes Sampaloc, Palakpakin and Pandin
column6: The project will develop and integrated land-use and lake-use management plan for the watershed surrounding Lakes Sampaloc, Palakpakin and Pandin. Using participatory approaches, it will assess the environemntal problems (e.g. water pollution, aquaculture productivity, fish diversity, water hyacinth, agricultural farm productivity and land use change etc.) faced by various stakeholders in each of the watershed of the three lakes. It will help the LGUs to evaluate environmental and socio-economic impacts of the future land-use and lake-use plan in each of the three lakes and prioritize management strategies to reduce the impacts of these changes. The results of the study will help identify policy options for sustainable watershed land- and lake-use management strategies and measures in the three lakes.

column4: SEVEN LAKES ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING PROGRAM: STRATEGIES TOWARD SUSTAINABLE LAKE ECOSYSTEM (7 LAMPS) - PHASE 2: Project 1. Surveillance of Invasive Alien Species in Tropical Maar Lakes: Biology and Ecology of Invasive Mollusks and Fish in the Lakes of San Pablo
column6:
Based on the study by Paller et al. (2017), there were several introduced fish species in the Seven Lakes of San Pablo City, Laguna including Carassius carassius,Channa striata, Cyprinus carpio, Oreochromis niloticus, Parachromis manguensis,
Red Nile Tilapia, and Vieja sp. Joshi (2006) noted that the biology, ecology and impacts of invasive alien species on native species such as the golden apple snail, Pomacea canaliculata, in the Philippines are poorly understood. This is due to lack of knowledge, lack of expensive and comprehensive technical information, failure to
realize the potential ecological damage to biodiversity and consequent economic losses and possible hazards to human health, failure of implementation of laws on introduction of exotic species, and unwillingness to interfere in the commerce and trade of exotic species. In addition, scarce data available on the impact of invasive
species reflect the lack of any common framework for quantifying the overall impacts of invasive species. This study will provide data on the morphological and molecular profile of invasive mollusks. included in the study were based on their use and trophic class: Sampaloc lake as eutrophic and both aquaculture and ecotourism lake, Yambo lake as oligotrophic and ecotourism lake, and Palakpakin lake as eutrophic and aquaculture lake.

column4: S&T INTERVENTION TOWARDS CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE ENDEMIC CYPRINIDS OF LAKE LANAO: Project 1. DNA Barcoding and Population Genetics of Lake Lanao Endemic Cyprinids
column6:
This project aims to conduct a comprehensive Lake Lanao endemic cyprinids inventory through DNA barcoding, and to publish their DNA barcode in public databases to serve as a reference sequence for future molecular identification. The project also aims to find areas of Lake Lanao that harbor stable populations of endemic cyprinids. Once these populations are identified, patterns of genetic diversity, relatedness, and divergence among the different populations of endemic cyprinids will be conducted using the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) control region (CR) or the cytochrome b (cyt b) gene and microsatellites
as markers. Genetic diversity indices and genetic differentiation of the different populations of the endemic cyprinids will be determined. These results will be used in formulating policies on the management and conservation of endemic cyprinids that will be suggested to the Local Government Units (LGUs) of Lanao del Sur and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Agrarian Reform (MAFAR) of Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao. column4: S&T INTERVENTION TOWARDS CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE ENDEMIC CYPRINIDS OF LAKE LANAO: Project 3. Bacterial Microbiota of Lake Lanao’s Endemic Cyprinids
column6: Samples of selected endemic cyprinid species in Lake Lanao will be investigated and assessed for their bacterial microbiota. The present study will be undertaken to quantitatively and qualitatively investigate the bacterial microbiota of selected endemic cyprinids and the water in Lake Lanao as an attempt to generate some baseline information on the normal flora of the selected endemic cyprinids and as basis in the formulation of pragmatic disease prevention and control strategies.

column4: S&T INTERVENTION TOWARDS CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE ENDEMIC CYPRINIDS OF LAKE LANAO: Project 4. Development of Non-Invasive Tool for Biomass Estimation of Endemic Cyprinids and Macrofauna Characterization of their Habitat
column6: Endemic cyprinids have been continuously impacted by various anthropogenic induced threats (i.e., climatic changes)--requiring conservation intervention to prevent further extinction and alleviate population decline. Proper management and conservation, however, needs understanding of key drivers of decline in biodiversity and knowledge of their causes. Specifically, we need to have an idea of how the population of endemic cyprinids change across time and space together with the knowledge of what other macrofauna they interact with--particularly, invasive species that can lead to their population decline. While traditional methods allow estimation of population size or biomass, they are mainly invasive or rely on fish catch data making these methods not suitable in abundance/biomass estimation for endemic species that we want to conserve. Similarly, popularity of citizen science that can address in characterizing biotic component of habitat, these efforts are limited to aquatic systems such as Lake Lanao. These data gap, which limits our capacity to formulate effective policy action for endemic cyprinids, mainly arise from the difficulty of documenting aquatic diversity particularly endemic cyprinids. Hence, developing method that will enable non-invasive estimation of endemic cyprinids biomass and characterization of their habitat is needed.

column4: S&T INTERVENTION TOWARDS CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT OF THE ENDEMIC CYPRINIDS OF LAKE LANAO: Project 5. Limnological Profiling of Lake Lanao Towards the Characterization of Endemic Cyprinids Habitat
column6: Lake Lanao in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), Philippines is one of the 17 ancient lakes of the world with a tectonic-volcanic origin. Lake Lanao is known for its endemic cyprinids. However, 15 of 17 reported endemic species have gone extinct, leaving only Puntius lindog and Puntius tumba critically endangered (Glorioso, 2020). The extinct endemic species were likely eaten by invasive species introduced into the lake according to IUCN. This project addresses critical gaps in the conservation and management of the remaining Lake Lanao endemic cyprinids by providing an updated limnological profile of Lake Lanao and GIS-based mapping tools. The GIS technology and data sets from the limnological profile can generate geo maps, habitat models, and data visualization to identify favorable habitats for fishing, analyze species distribution, and identify threats from invasive species. This approach will help identify high-priority conservation sites and potential risks to cyprinid ecosystems.

column4: EASTERN VISAYAS BIRTH COHORT: NUTRITION AND MULTI-OMICS DETERMINANTS OF CHILDREN’S GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT: Project 3. Infant Gut Microbiota and Linear Growth: A Longitudinal Study of the Eastern Visayas Birth Cohort
column6:
Stunting is common indicator of undernutrition prevalent among children under-age of five globally. It is the result of inadequate nutrition and recurrent infection, which is irreversible if no interventions took place in the first 1000 days of life. This leads to a significant impediment in child growth and development that may impair the human capital in society.

Recent evidence has shown the relationship of gut microbiota to human nutrition. The proposed study aims to determine the changes in gut microbial diversity and associate it with growth, diet, and morbidity during the first 1000 days of life. In this, samples at birth up to 2 years of age will be collected since the gut microbiota development and colonization suggest beginning at birth. Pregnant women on their third trimester will be recruited and screened to be eligible participants. Infants will be collected with fecal samples, anthropometry, and food diary at multiple sampling points (0-3-6-12-24 months). DNA extraction up to 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing will be conducted from the fecal samples, and afterward, these data will be analyzed using different tools. Profiling the gut microbial diversity of infants at multiple time points from age 0 to 2 years old and correlating it to growth (length‐for‐age/height‐for‐age z‐scores), diet and morbidity are the objectives of the study. Also, determining the role of the gut microbiota early in life may lead to a better understanding of the etiology and pathophysiology of stunting.

column4: DERISKING THE TUKLAS LUNAS PIPELINES: ADMET ASSAYS FOR FOR BRIDGING EFFICACY AND SAFETY (ADMET PHASE II): Project 2. Cell-based ADMET assays
column6:
Tuklas Lunas projects across the country — many of which seek to leverage Philippine biodiversity — follow the downstream steps of synthetic combinatorial library screening as they approach purification and structure elucidation steps. To de-risk candidate compounds, they are subjected to iterative structure activity relationship studies during lead optimization to confer drug-like features.
At this step, compounds are tested for multiple organ toxicity, ability to cross the gastro-intestinal tract, whether or not they are pumped out by efflux transporters, or whether they inhibit or activate CYP450 drug metabolizing enzymes – a cause of treatment failures or adverse reactions. The ADMET Phase I program was able to optimize and pilot three other toxicity assays (skeletal, neuronal and endothelial cell toxicity) required by regulatory authorities on top of hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity and cardiotoxicity assays that have already been used to test thousands of samples. Permeability and efflux assays as well as CYP 450 induction and inhibition assays have also been optimized. Two assays are on the final optimization of the remaining parameters in the next month. All these assays will be performed on samples submitted by other research groups during Phase II to identify optimized lead compounds with the most desirable drug-like features for further development.
